direction.name: Differentiable pool multipath channel model + learned beacon localization on the Orin

proposal.one_line_claim: A 4-hydrophone AUV can localize an audio-band beacon in 3D (not just bearing) inside a reverberant 25 m pool by fitting a differentiable image-source model of the pool (learnable per-wall reflection filters, hydrophone geometry, speaker response, inter-board clock offset) to ~40 known-pose chirp recordings, then using that fitted model as both the likelihood for a GPU grid-search localizer and the simulator for a small learned localizer running in real time on the Jetson AGX Orin; wall echoes supply the range information that 3 TDOAs on a sub-30 cm baseline cannot.
proposal.method: Observable: per-channel channel impulse responses (CIRs) obtained by matched-filtering each 96 kHz channel against the transmitted 50 ms, 2-18 kHz linear chirp (compressed pulse ~60 us = 9 cm, so surface/bottom/wall echoes are resolvable out to ~15 m). Forward model (PyTorch, batched on GPU): Allen-Berkley shoebox image-source method for the measured LxWxD pool, order <=2 (125 images; order 3 as an ablation), plus a single tilted bottom plane at order 1 if the floor slopes. Image k reaches hydrophone m at delay |s_k - r_m|/c + delta_b(m) with amplitude 1/|s_k - r_m| times the product of the wall filters along its path; rendered in the frequency domain as e^{-j w tau} times filter products, summed, IFFT -> 4 synthetic CIRs. Learnable parameters: (i) six per-wall reflection filters, each 2-3 cascaded state-variable biquads evaluated by frequency sampling (Lee 2022 Sec. III; surface fixed at -1), shared across all images touching that wall, with |R|<=1 penalty (Chitre eq. 21); (ii) speaker response as a differentiable PEQ; (iii) hydrophone positions r_m (init from CAD, L2 prior +-3 cm), gains, and a 16-tap per-channel FIR absorbing hull scattering; (iv) per-board clock offset and drift delta_b (only if the clock problem is not solved in hardware); (v) sound speed c and wall-position error terms (+-5 cm prior); (vi) source position p, known during fitting, free during localization. Loss: multi-resolution STFT log-magnitude (256/512/1024) on the CIR envelopes, plus a complex L1 term on the first 1.5 ms window (direct + surface arrivals) added after envelope convergence (coarse-to-fine, because cm-level geometry errors destroy phase agreement at 10 kHz but not envelope agreement), plus Chitre-style L2 penalties on the geometric error terms. Fit: ~40 known-pose recordings, Adam, laptop GPU, minutes. Localization A (MAP): evaluate the fitted model's loss over a 10 cm 3D grid (~1e5 points, batched on the Orin), Nelder-Mead refine. Localization B (learned): small CNN on 4-channel GCC-PHAT maps plus stacked CIR envelopes -> (x,y,z), trained on ~50k renders from the fitted model with randomized p, SNR and mixed-in recorded thruster noise, fine-tuned on real poses, exported TensorRT FP16. Same frames go to GCC-PHAT, SRP-PHAT and MUSIC baselines. Sanity check of the renderer against pyroomacoustics with c=1480 before any pool time.
proposal.experiment_plan: Session 0 (lab, weeks 1-2, no pool): (a) inject one electrical click train into one channel of each Daisy board for 10 min and measure inter-board sample drift (ppm) and USB start offset; this decides the clock fix. (b) Speaker characterization in a bucket/tank at 10-20 cm with one hydrophone: WAV vs any codec, frequency response 1-20 kHz, THD at three volumes, directivity at 0/45/90 deg, playback-clock offset from chirp time-scaling. (c) End-to-end pipeline latency on the Orin with synthetic data. Pool session 1 (fit set, ~3 h, thrusters off): sub static on the pool floor at a taped position near the deep-end centre, heading aligned to a lane line. Speaker on a marked PVC pole at fixed orientation (facing down). Transmit file: 10 s loop of twenty 50 ms 2-18 kHz chirps at 0.5 s spacing, 1 s silence, one 1 s pink burst. Person 1 walks the pole to grid positions (ranges 1-15 m along 3 lanes, depths 0.5/1.0/1.5 m), person 2 reads tape from two walls and depth mark and logs, person 3 runs recording on the Orin and checks levels. ~40 poses at ~3 min each, then ~10 poses with thrusters at two fixed PWM levels for self-noise. Record water temperature (c changes ~3 m/s per degree C). Pool session 2 (eval set, ~3 h): ~40 new poses including a held-out range band (>12 m) and depths not in the fit set; move the sub to a second floor position rotated 90 deg and record ~15 poses to test whether the fitted model transfers to a new receiver pose; one continuous slow walk of the pole for tracking. Pool session 3 (optional, contingency/repeat). Ground truth: tape from two walls (+-5 cm), pole depth marks (+-2 cm), sub heading from lane line (+-3 deg); optionally a GoPro above with tags. Total ~100 static poses plus one walk. Metrics: azimuth and elevation MAE, 3D position error and range error (median, 90th percentile) binned by range (0-5, 5-10, 10-15, >15 m) and by SNR (real thruster-on poses plus offline mixing of recorded thruster noise), miss rate; model quality as log-spectral distance and predicted-vs-measured echo delays on held-out poses; on the Orin: per-frame latency, throughput, and power (tegrastats/jtop) at MAXN and 15 W. Central ablation: the same learned localizer trained on (a) free-field simulation as in Song 2025, (b) a generic shoebox with guessed reflection coefficients, (c) the fitted model; the paper's claim stands or falls on (c) beating (a) and (b) on real pool data. Honest expectation: azimuth gains over GCC-PHAT on a windowed direct path will be small; the headline should be range/3D error, where TDOA-only cannot compete on this baseline.
baselines: GCC-PHAT TDOA + least-squares bearing (windowed direct path), the standard USBL-style method (Song 2025 and Kasetkasem 2017 both benchmark against it)
SRP-PHAT on the same 10 cm 3D grid (fair comparison to the MAP localizer, same compute budget)
Narrowband MUSIC per frequency bin (4 elements, coherent multipath will degrade it; included because reviewers expect it)
Single-hydrophone multipath ranging from direct/surface/bottom echo delays (Li 2016 / Wang 2018 recipe with two reflectors) as the range baseline
Learned localizer trained on free-field simulation only (Song 2025 recipe) and on an un-fitted generic shoebox, to quantify the sim2real gap the fitted model closes
Kasetkasem 2017 OMP sparse multipath decomposition then first-arrival bearing (multipath-as-nuisance baseline)

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Ray-basis neural network: differentiable image-source/ray model with learnable image-source position errors and a shared reflection-coefficient NN, trained on sparse CW (10 kHz) amplitude measurements; validated with a single hydrophone in a 2.5 m fiberglass tank, achieving Spearman 0.96 against GPR/DNN baselines that failed; noted strong sensitivity of multi-reflection fits to minor wall irregularities and needed a second stage to estimate position errors.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: We fit broadband time-domain CIRs (2-18 kHz chirps) with per-wall frequency-dependent reflection filters rather than CW amplitude; a 4-channel vehicle-mounted array with learnable hydrophone geometry and clock offset rather than a single moved hydrophone; and the fitted model is used downstream for localization and as a training simulator on an embedded GPU. Chitre's group (also OCEANS Limerick 2023 'Differentiable ocean acoustic propagation modeling', not in our corpus) will likely review; position as an application of their recipe to array localization in a bounded environment, and cite both.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Differentiable artificial reverberation: replaced IIR components (state-variable biquads, delay networks) with frequency-sampled FIR approximations so reverb parameters can be trained end-to-end with a multi-scale STFT loss; trained on 200k shoebox image-source RIRs; room acoustics for speech/music.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: We borrow the frequency-sampled differentiable SVF filters and multi-resolution STFT loss, but our model is a physical image-source geometry of a specific water volume whose parameters mean something (wall reflectance, hydrophone positions), and the target task is localization, not perceptual reverb matching.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: 3-element array on a compact vehicle, STFT phase-difference maps into a saliency-aware ConvLSTM, trained on 10k synthetic samples from a delay+attenuation+noise model with no multipath, lake trial at 80-97 m: 4.97 deg MAE vs 13.46 deg for GCC; inference on a SOPHON X3-Pi edge board at 0.8 s per 1 s segment.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: They estimate azimuth only, train multipath-free, and test in a low-reverberation lake; we estimate 3D position, train on a fitted multipath model, and test in a highly reverberant pool, reporting latency and power on a CUDA GPU. Note: this paper contradicts the survey's claim that no hydrophone DL runs on an edge device; our novelty is GPU + multipath-aware + 3D, not 'first edge'.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Pinger bearing with a 4-hydrophone 2 cm square array; OMP sparse decomposition of the received pulse into multipath copies, then subspace bearing per path, taking the first arrival; simulation plus real data with a 30 kHz Teledyne pinger in the Kasetsart University swimming pool.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: They treat multipath as a nuisance to be separated and discarded and never use pool geometry; we model the pool explicitly and use the echoes for range. Their real pool experiment means the survey's 'no DOA in pools' claim is wrong; cite them as the multipath-as-nuisance baseline.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Single-hydrophone 3D localization of whale calls by matched-impulse-response processing of unresolved overlapping multipath against a bathymetry-based propagation model (OCEANS 2017 Aberdeen).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Same idea in spirit (match the whole multipath IR to a model rather than pick arrivals), but their model is fixed and ocean-scale; ours is learned from data in a bounded volume, uses an array, and runs on the vehicle. Cite as the closest matched-IR localization precedent, and note it was an Aberdeen paper.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Single-hydrophone range from the direct-to-surface-reflected delay obtained by autocorrelation and compared with model predictions (reliable acoustic path); related work 8604304 (Wang 2018) and 11085563 (Li 2025) extend to surface+bottom arrivals.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: These use two reflectors and a fixed propagation model; a pool has six reflectors and we learn their filters. Our range baseline is exactly their method.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: TDOA localization robust to sensor position uncertainty via ridge-regularized weighted total least squares (OCEANS 2026 Sanya).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: We handle hydrophone position error by making positions learnable during model fitting (self-calibration from known-pose data) rather than by a robust estimator at inference time; complementary, cite for the array-uncertainty framing.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Underwater source localization pretrained on simulated data and fine-tuned on limited measured data with supervised contrastive learning (OCEANS 2026 Sanya).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Same sim-then-real recipe, but their simulator is generic; our simulator is fit to the very environment being tested, and our ablation directly measures how much that fit closes the sim2real gap.

hardware_blockers: Two Daisy Seed boards with independent crystals: at 96 kHz, a 20-50 ppm frequency offset is 2-5 samples/s of drift (20-50 us/s) plus an arbitrary USB stream start offset; 10 us is already 1.5 cm of path, so cross-board TDOA is meaningless without a fix. Within one 50 ms chirp drift is ~1 us (fine); the problem is the per-frame offset. Options in order of speed: (a) replace both boards with one class-compliant 4-input USB audio interface at 96-192 kHz (~$150-200, works on the Orin via ALSA; fastest and most robust); (b) modify libDaisy so board B's SAI runs as I2S slave to board A's MCLK/BCLK/LRCLK over three wires (real firmware work, 1-2 weeks); (c) inject a shared electrical click into one channel of each board (costs SNR on that channel, gives a per-second offset); (d) learnable offset+drift inside the model works only when the source pose is known (calibration) and is ambiguous with source position at deployment, so it is a fallback, not a solution. Decide by end of week 2 after measuring actual drift.

Speaker band <=20 kHz and uncalibrated: no validation at the 25-40 kHz RoboSub pinger band, so the RoboSub tie-in is by analogy only; use WAV files, not MP3 (codec destroys chirp phase); check whether the speaker's internal DSP compresses or band-limits; expect strong resonant peaks and directivity above ~5 kHz, so keep its orientation fixed across poses and model its response as a learnable PEQ; playback clock offset time-scales the chirp by ppm (negligible within a chirp, but chirp detection must be data-driven, not scheduled); no absolute time of emission, so absolute range must come from echo structure, which is the point of the paper but also its limit (surface-echo delay falls to ~67 us at 20 m range with 1 m depths, at the 60 us resolution floor).

Hull-mounted hydrophones: near-field scattering and shadowing by the hull break the free-field array manifold; baseline likely <30 cm so elevation is weakly observable from TDOA; thruster self-noise and possible electrical noise from the sub's power electronics. The learnable per-channel FIR absorbs some of this, but it is a real error source for MUSIC/SRP as well.

Pool geometry unknown: length, width, depth profile (sloped floor breaks the shoebox assumption; handled by a tilted bottom plane at order 1 or by working in the flat deep end), overflow gutters and lane ropes at the surface, wall material; sound speed varies ~3 m/s per degree C so water temperature must be logged per session; pool booking time is the schedule constraint (need 2-3 sessions of ~3 h).

Ground truth: needs a marked PVC pole, tape measures, and a way to fix and record the sub's position and heading (taped floor marks, lane lines); ~5 cm / 3 deg accuracy is achievable and sufficient given expected 10-30 cm localization error.

Orin deployment: the grid-search and fractional-delay rendering must be written as plain torch ops to export to TensorRT; power measurement requires jtop/tegrastats and running at fixed power modes; the existing whisper_ivc streaming stack must be extended to 4 synchronized channels.
proposal.track: Track 02 Sonar Signal/Image Processing & Communication (array processing + ML on the vehicle is the headline); Track 01 Underwater Acoustics is the fallback if the fitted-channel-model contribution is emphasized over localization. Also enter the Student Poster Competition with the same abstract.

evidence: Ribeiro, Ba, Zhang, Florencio, 'Turning enemies into friends: Using reflections to improve sound source localization', ICME 2010 (IEEE arnumber 5583886): compact array + integrated loudspeaker self-probes to estimate ceiling height and wall positions, then a maximum-likelihood SSL that uses an image-source model of the early reflections; explicitly shows early reflections 'significantly improve range and elevation estimation' for a small array. This is the proposal's core physical claim ('wall echoes supply the range information that 3 TDOAs on a sub-30 cm baseline cannot') done 16 years ago in air, including the self-calibration step. The survey line 'Nobody has exploited that' (00_directions.md sec 1.1) is false as written.

Wang et al., 'Hearing Anything Anywhere' / DiffRIR, CVPR 2024 (arXiv 2406.07532, dataset on Zenodo 11195833): differentiable, interpretable parametric RIR renderer fit to ~12 measured RIRs with a learned per-surface frequency-dependent reflection response and a learned direction-dependent source response, then used as a simulator to render responses at novel poses. That is items (i)+(ii) of the proposal's learnable-parameter list and the 'fitted model as simulator' use, in air. Also Zhi & Sharma, 'A Differentiable Image Source Model for Room Acoustics Optimization', WASPAA 2023 (IEEE 10248140), and Yu & Kleijn, arXiv 2301.09198 (2023), which jointly estimate source position, receiver position, room geometry and reflection coefficients from a single RIR.

Localization A (evaluate a propagation model over a 3D grid and pick the best match) is matched-field processing. MFP in reverberant tanks with reflections modelled is published: Dowling group, Bartlett MFP in a reverberant cylindrical tank (1.07 m dia x 0.8 m), 16 hydrophones, 20-120 kHz, replica includes direct, once- and multiply-reflected paths (found via search; JASA-family); 'Broadband match-field processing applied in a highly reverberant environment' (ResearchGate 260924024). Yangzhou, Ma, Huang, 'A deep neural network approach to acoustic source localization in a shallow water tank experiment', JASA 146(6):4802, 2019, DOI 10.1121/1.5138596: DNN localizer in a reflective shallow tank, trained on measured tank data, benchmarked against MFP and normal-mode MUSIC. So 'DL localizer in a reverberant tank vs MFP/MUSIC baselines' exists.

Kari, Zhuang, Singer, 'Mismatch-Robust Underwater Acoustic Localization Using a Differentiable Modular Forward Model', arXiv 2503.23260 (Mar 2025, ONR-funded): differentiable, physics-modular multipath forward model (learns path lengths of the multipath structure end-to-end), gradient-based source localization, network weights re-optimised at inference to absorb environment mismatch. Simulation-only, but it is exactly 'differentiable multipath forward model as localization likelihood, underwater'. Together with Chitre, 'Differentiable Ocean Acoustic Propagation Modeling', OCEANS 2023 Limerick (UnderwaterAcoustics.jl) and Li & Chitre 10224658 (tank-validated data-aided ray model), the 'differentiable underwater propagation model fit to data' idea is established and its authors are likely reviewers.

Misiurewicz et al., 'Multipath Propagation of Acoustic Signal in a Swimming Pool - Source Localization Problem', Sensors 22(3):1162, 2022, DOI 10.3390/s22031162: 4 hydrophones, 25 x 12.5 m sport pool, deterministic + random multipath models, TDOA localization with multi-hypothesis testing over wall/bottom reflection paths. Pool + 4 hydrophones + explicit multipath modelling for localization already exists (wall-mounted, not vehicle-mounted).

Learned localizer trained on simulated multipath then applied to real data: Ferguson, Williams, Jin, 'Sound Source Localization in a Multipath Environment Using CNNs', ICASSP 2018 (arXiv 1710.10948); Ferguson et al. ICASSP 2017 (IEEE 7952638) single-sensor cepstrum CNN ranging from multipath; Song 2025 (11104616); Yan 2026 (11616801) sim-pretrain + real fine-tune; Ocean Engineering 353:124715 (2026) DeepONet localization in confined underwater environments with wall reverberation. The corpus search 'multipath pool' returning zero hits reflects IEEE Xplore coverage, not the literature.

Nothing found that does the full conjunction: vehicle-mounted 4-element sub-30 cm array + differentiable image-source model of a real pool fit from broadband CIRs + fitted model used both as MFP replica and as training simulator + on-vehicle GPU inference with latency/power. The novelty is the conjunction and the sim2real ablation, not any component.
votes.fix: Drop every 'first' and 'nobody has exploited' phrasing; the paper will be reviewed by people who know Ribeiro 2010, DiffRIR, Dowling's tank MFP and Chitre/Singer. Reposition P1 explicitly as: 'matched-field localization with a data-fitted differentiable replica model for a vehicle-mounted short-baseline array in a reverberant pool, and a measurement of how much environment-specific fitting closes the sim2real gap for a learned localizer on an embedded GPU'. Make the central ablation (free-field sim vs generic shoebox vs fitted pool model, same CNN, same real eval set) the headline contribution, because that quantity has not been reported for hydrophone arrays; report range/3D error vs range band where TDOA-only fails, as the plan already says. Cite Ribeiro 2010 and DiffRIR up front as the in-air precedents and state the underwater deltas honestly: 25 m scale (echo delays of ms not hundreds of us), hull-scattered array manifold, no shared clock, uncalibrated consumer source, thruster noise, and a fitted-then-deployed model running on the vehicle with latency/power numbers. Cite Kari-Zhuang-Singer 2025 and Chitre 2023 as the differentiable-underwater-model precedents and position the pool as the first real-data test of that recipe on an AUV array. Cite Misiurewicz 2022 as the existing 25 m pool multipath localization baseline and Yangzhou 2019 as the tank DL-vs-MFP precedent. Keep Track 02 (systems + array processing + edge ML); the model-fitting contribution alone will not survive in Track 01 against DiffRIR/Chitre. Secondary defensible claims: joint learning of inter-board clock offset and hydrophone geometry during calibration (minor), and the open labelled dataset (P0), which becomes more important as insurance given the crowded method space.

votes.lens: Feasibility / pool-test engineering (3 people, 3 sessions, uncalibrated speaker, unsynced Daisy boards, Orin)
evidence: Scope vs. calendar: the proposal bundles (1) a hardware/firmware clock fix, (2) speaker characterization, (3) a differentiable image-source renderer + fit, (4) a GPU MAP localizer, (5) a CNN localizer trained on 50k renders + real fine-tune + TensorRT export, (6) six baselines incl. OMP/MUSIC/SRP, (7) Orin latency/power at two power modes, and (8) 2-3 pool sessions, all before a 7 Dec 2026 abstract (13 weeks from today, 2026-09-06) with 3 students who also run a RoboSub vehicle. That is ~15-18 focused person-weeks of engineering before any result; the plan's own 'weeks_to_first_result=8' assumes nothing slips (pool booking, hull re-seal, firmware).

Clock: 96 kHz with two free-running crystals (20-50 ppm) = 20-50 us/s relative drift plus an arbitrary USB start offset; 10 us = 1.5 cm of path, so cross-board TDOA is unusable without a hardware fix. The two viable fixes (class-compliant 4-in USB interface with plug-in/phantom power for the Aquarian H2a, or libDaisy SAI-slave firmware) both require opening and re-integrating the sealed hull before pool session 1; the 'learnable offset' fallback is ambiguous with source position at deployment, as the proposal itself concedes. This is equipment/firmware we do not currently have working.

Ground truth: tape-from-two-walls at 10-20 m across open water plus a hand-held pole at 0.5-1.5 m depth (3 deg of pole tilt = 8 cm at 1.5 m) gives realistic +-10-15 cm horizontal, not +-5 cm; the sub must be placed by free-diving at a taped mark on the deep-end floor (3-4 m) with +-5 cm / +-3 deg. That GT budget is the same size as the 10-30 cm 3D error the paper wants to headline, so the median-3D-error claim is GT-limited. Chitre 2023 (10224658, Table VII/VIII, Sec. IV-B) shows their fit quality degrades with position measurement error, phase far more than amplitude, and needed a second training stage just to estimate per-point position errors even in a 2.5 m tank with a reel-and-fishing-line positioner.

Physics of the ranging claim: with the receiver on the floor the bottom image is nearly coincident with the direct arrival (13-40 us at D=2 m, below the 60 us compressed-pulse resolution), so it is not an independent range cue; the surface-direct delay is 165-294 us at 15 m with a slope of only -10 to -18 us/m, i.e. sub-resolution delay interpolation (~5 us) is needed to get <0.5 m range from the surface echo alone. Range must therefore come from side-wall images, which depend on the source's lateral position and on wall irregularities (gutters, lane ropes, ladders, steps, sloped floor). Chitre 2023 Sec. IV: 'multiple reflections lead to strong sensitivity to minor geometrical irregularities of the tank wall' in a 2.5 m fiberglass tank at 10 kHz; a 25 m concrete pool is far worse and an order<=2 shoebox (125 images) cannot represent a CIR that in a 2-3.5 m deep pool contains ~5 near-equal-amplitude vertical orders within the first 5 ms after direct and a reverberant tail of ~3 s (Sabine estimate); a full-length multi-res STFT envelope loss will be dominated by un-modelled late reverb.

Speaker: consumer SD-card pool speakers decode MP3/WAV through a cheap codec chip (typ. 44.1/48 kHz, hard low-pass ~16 kHz) into a class-D amp and a resonant transducer; directivity above ~5 kHz plus a hand-held pole means the effective source response changes pose-to-pose by more than the learnable PEQ can absorb unless orientation is fixed to ~+-10 deg, which a person walking a pole 25 m cannot hold. Surface ripples from people moving around the pool make the surface echo time-varying within a 3 min pose (Chitre reports fluctuations from a light breeze and averaged over 40 s).

Orin real-time MAP is under-costed by ~100x: 1e5 grid points x 4 channels x 8192 bins x 125 images = 0.4 T complex MACs per frame (6.6 T for the ~2000 images a shallow pool actually needs). At a realistic 2-5 TFLOPS FP32 on the AGX Orin that is 0.2-3 s per frame, not 'real time' for 2 Hz chirps; a hierarchical search or a delay-domain lookup is required.

Learned localizer claim is narrower than stated: the CNN is trained on renders for ONE receiver pose (sub taped to the floor). Song 2025 (11104616) already shows a sim-trained DOA net degrades outside its training coverage ('performance drops when testing at azimuths outside the model's training range'); a net trained for one hull pose in one pool is a fixed-pool positioning system, not 'AUV localization', and the session-2 '90 deg rotated' test will expose this. The proposal's central ablation (fitted vs free-field vs generic shoebox) rests on ~40-55 real eval poses, all from 1-2 receiver poses.

Logistics: 40 poses x 3 min = 2 h of pure recording in a 3 h booking that also includes placing/taping the sub by free-diving, waiting for water to settle, and level checks; expect 25-30 usable poses per session, not 40. The sub must sit powered on the floor for 3 h with the Orin recording: battery-limited unless tethered; a mid-session battery swap costs ~30+ min of hull open/re-seal. Kasetkasem 2017 (8096292) managed only 5 pinger positions in their pool experiment with a 192 kHz SHARC DAQ; that is the realistic density reviewers have seen from pool DOA work.

Reviewer acceptance: pool/tank results are accepted at OCEANS (Kasetkasem 2017 pool, Chitre 2023 tank, Barazzutti 2017 Aberdeen), so the venue is not the blocker; the blocker is that the headline metric (median 3D error) will be within the ground-truth noise and the deployed component (CNN) only works for a static receiver.
votes.fix: Keep the direction but cut it to what 3 sessions and pool ground truth can actually support, in this order: (1) Solve the clock in hardware before anything else (single 4-channel USB interface or SAI-slave firmware), and measure the residual drift as a reported result; do not ship the 'learnable offset' as a contribution. (2) Replace the full order-2/3 shoebox fit with an 'early-reflection self-calibration' model: direct + surface + floor + the 4 first-order side-wall images (and optionally 2nd-order vertical) with learnable hydrophone body-frame positions, per-channel gain/FIR, per-wall reflection filter, sound speed and wall-offset terms, fitted only on a windowed early CIR (first ~10-20 ms after direct) with the envelope-then-phase coarse-to-fine loss; this keeps the differentiable/DDSP novelty and Chitre/Lee lineage without needing an order-10 model that wall irregularities will break. (3) Make the MAP localizer (coarse 1 m grid -> local refine, delay-domain lookup, plain torch ops) the deployed estimator on the Orin and report its latency/power; drop the CNN localizer and TensorRT from the headline paper, or reduce it to a single ablation row ('fitted-sim-trained net vs free-field-sim-trained net on real data') without the real-time claim. (4) Budget ground truth honestly: use a taut marked line along a lane rope for along-pool distance, a rigid pole with a depth stop and a bubble level, an above-water camera with a tag on the pole top, log water temperature; report range error in 0.5 m bins and azimuth/elevation in degrees, and state the GT budget (+-10 cm, +-3 deg) in the paper so the range/3D numbers are not read as sub-GT. (5) Plan for 25-30 poses per session, 2 s chirp spacing (pool RT60 ~3 s), fixed speaker orientation via a clamp on the pole, thrusters-off fit set, and tether power for the sub. (6) Headline claim becomes: 'Self-calibrated early-reflection channel model from a hull-mounted 4-hydrophone array in a reverberant pool enables 3D (bearing + coarse range) beacon localization on the vehicle GPU, vs GCC-PHAT bearing + single-hydrophone surface-echo range (Li 2016)'; keep P0 (dataset) as the insurance abstract and enter the Student Poster Competition with the same data. With that narrowing the 7 Dec abstract needs only session 1 + fit + MAP, which is achievable in ~10 weeks if the clock fix lands by week 3.

direction.name: Audio-band chirp-spread-spectrum inter-vehicle link from a consumer speaker, GPU demodulation, packets double as TDOA beacons

proposal.one_line_claim: A LoRa-style chirp-spread-spectrum broadcast link transmitted by an unmodified consumer underwater speaker (SD-card playback, 3-16 kHz), received on a 4-hydrophone AUV array and decoded in real time on the vehicle's Jetson Orin with a preamble-trained, reverberation-aware dechirp that turns pool wall echoes from symbol errors into a matched-filter gain, where every packet preamble also yields the transmitter's bearing (and clock-offset-corrected cross-board TDOA) without any extra beacon hardware.
proposal.method:
TX: pre-rendered 96 kHz WAV files on the speaker's SD card (never Bluetooth). Frame = 8 up-chirp preamble + 2.25 down-chirp SFD + N data symbols, LoRa frequency-shift chirp modulation (Vangelista 2017 / Steinmetz 9905674), Gray-coded, plus a CRC-16 and a short Hamming(7,4) or simple repetition option. Band chosen from a Week-1 speaker sweep: expect fc ~ 9-10 kHz, BW 4-8 kHz; SF in {6,7,8,9} gives Tsym 8-128 ms at BW 4 kHz and 30-500 bit/s. Preamble uses SF+1 vs data (Steinmetz's own suggested fix for sync failures). TX-side pre-equalisation of the measured speaker magnitude response, exactly as Steinmetz did for the AS-1 hydrophone.

RX on Orin (PyTorch/CuPy, batched over 4 channels): bandpass, complex baseband shift to fc, decimate to fs=BW, sliding dechirp + FFT for preamble detection with CA-CFAR (Steinmetz), SFD for STO/CFO. The new piece: in a static pool the channel's delay taps at tau_k map, after dechirp, to fixed bin offsets round(tau_k*BW) with fixed gains - i.e. the dechirp magnitude spectrum of every data symbol is the ideal single-bin spike circularly convolved with a channel 'bin profile' h[b]. Estimate h[b] from the 8 known preamble symbols (average their dechirp spectra, they are symbol 0), then decode each data symbol by circular cross-correlation of its dechirp spectrum with h[b] and argmax - a RAKE/matched filter in the dechirp domain, costing one extra FFT per symbol. Combine 4 channels by summing the per-channel correlation scores (non-coherent diversity; per-board coherent combining is a second variant). Baselines: plain argmax dechirp (Steinmetz/DeWater baseline); a small CNN/ConvNeXt or DeWater-style learned demod on dechirp spectrograms trained on P1's fitted image-source simulator and fine-tuned on pool recordings.

Localization: GCC-PHAT on the preamble between the two same-board hydrophone pairs gives two exact TDOAs (bearing cones); cross-board TDOAs use a per-board clock offset/drift estimated from an in-band electrical sync pulse (see blockers), then hyperbolic LS for 2-D position at known speaker depth. Output: decoded payload + bearing + latency/power (jtop) per packet.
proposal.experiment_plan:
Pre-pool (bench, Week 1-2): speaker in a bucket/tank with one hydrophone 30 cm away: log-sweep 0.5-24 kHz, THD at 3 levels, SD-card WAV vs MP3 vs Bluetooth, DAC sample-rate error (measure chirp-rate mismatch); Daisy board clock drift measurement (feed the same tone to both boards for 10 min, track phase). Deliverable: usable band, SF/BW table, ppm figures.

Pool session 1 (3 people, 3 h, 'link + calibration'): sub static on the bottom at one marked spot (or clamped to a ladder), hydrophone positions measured to 1 cm. Speaker on a weighted line from a pole at ~30 marked lane/deck positions (tape-measure grid, phone photo from a fixed overhead tripod for +/-5 cm ground truth, fixed depth ~1 m). Each pose plays one 90 s SD file: pilot chirp for channel/RIR, then 6 frames at each SF 6/7/8/9 with known random payloads (~2000 symbols per pose). Repeat 10 poses with thrusters at 30% and 60%. Roles: one moves speaker and calls positions, one runs Orin logging, one logs/photos. Record raw 4-ch 96 kHz; everything else is offline first.

Pool session 2 ('eval + realtime'): 20 new poses including 5 in corners/near walls (worst delay spread) and 5 with the sub slowly translating (0.2-0.5 m/s, Doppler + drift stress), real-time decode on Orin with latency and power logged; short text messages end-to-end for the Whisper comparison: same sentences (a) spoken through the speaker as raw audio and transcribed by the existing Whisper IVC, (b) sent as text over CSS.

Metrics: sync rate, SER/BER vs SF, vs pose class (open/near-wall/corner), vs thruster state, vs artificially added recorded thruster noise (SNR sweep, DeWater/Steinmetz style); effective bit/s; packet-preamble bearing error (deg) and 2-D position error (m) vs ground truth with and without cross-board sync; Orin latency (ms/packet) and power (W) for classic vs reverberation-aware vs learned decoder; WER of Whisper-over-raw-audio vs character error rate of text-over-CSS at matched pose/thruster conditions. Honest expectation: SNR will be high at all pool ranges, so the informative axes are delay spread and thruster noise, not distance.
baselines: Plain LoRa dechirp argmax receiver (Steinmetz 9905674 implementation, single channel and 4-channel sum)
JANUS-style or simple BFSK/DPSK at the same band and rate rendered through the same speaker (reference PHY, JANUS 3.0 Matlab port)
Learned demodulator on dechirp spectrograms (DeWater 11571741 style Swin/ConvNeXt, or lighter CNN) pre-trained on the P1 image-source pool simulator, fine-tuned on pool data
GCC-PHAT / SRP-PHAT bearing from preamble (classical), with and without clock-offset correction
Existing Whisper-over-raw-audio IVC (WER) vs text-over-CSS (CER) at matched conditions (the Rong 11104740 comparison)

Their band and hardware are unreachable for us; our contribution is orthogonal, not a better modem.

closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Same 'commodity transmitter + learned demod' spirit and the strongest competitor. hardware_blockers: Two Daisy Seed boards with independent crystals: expect tens of ppm relative drift (at 96 kHz that is several samples per second, i.e. ~50 us/s of TDOA drift, ~7 cm of path difference per second) plus an arbitrary start offset. Cross-board TDOA is therefore unusable without continuous sync. Recommended fix (1-2 days, small hardware mod): drive a short out-of-band electrical sync burst (e.g. 30-40 kHz, 1 Hz, from one Daisy's line output or an Orin GPIO) through a 100 k summing resistor into channel 1 of BOTH boards; matched-filter it in software to get offset and drift to sub-sample precision every second. Alternative with zero soldering: a hull-mounted piezo clicker at a known position heard by all four hydrophones. Fallback (software only): treat offset+drift as a nuisance parameter estimated jointly with 2-D position at known speaker depth - note per-packet 3-D localisation with an unknown offset is underdetermined (4 receivers give 3 TDOAs; unknowns are 3 coordinates + offset), so the fallback only works with fixed depth or multi-packet batches. Comms itself is unaffected: decode per channel and combine scores, never coherently across boards.

Speaker band and fidelity: consumer pool speakers typically have usable output only ~1-16 kHz with strong resonances and unknown THD; chirps must sit in the flat-ish part (likely 4-14 kHz) and be pre-equalised. If the player only accepts MP3, the codec will damage chirps at high SF/low BW; must confirm WAV playback and that the player does not auto-gain or fade. The player's own DAC clock error (~100 ppm) appears as a chirp-rate mismatch; measure it in Week 1 and compensate in the RX chirp template.

Speaker cannot receive: link is one-way broadcast only, so no two-way ranging, no ARQ, no clock sync between TX and RX -> the 'ranging' half of comm+ranging is bearing (and cross-board TDOA position) only; absolute range would require the P1 multipath model or a second sub. Frame it as broadcast beacon/telemetry, not a network.

Pool reverberation: 25 m concrete pool ~1.5-2 m deep with water-air surface (reflection ~ -1) and concrete walls (|R| ~ 0.7); delay spread of tens of ms with echoes within a few dB of the direct path. For LoRa dechirp every echo at delay tau appears as a peak at bin offset tau*BW, i.e. as a different symbol - this is the failure mode, not noise. Need SF high enough that Tsym >> delay spread (SF 8-9 at BW 4 kHz gives 64-128 ms) and the reverberation-aware decoder; symbol rate will be low (tens to ~300 bit/s). Also thruster wash near the hydrophones may exceed the speaker's level at low frequencies.

Ground truth: no tracking system; tape-measure grid + overhead phone camera gives ~5 cm, adequate for bearing accuracy claims (a few degrees at 5-15 m) but position errors below ~10 cm cannot be claimed. Speaker depth must be fixed and measured.
Orin data path: hydrophone->Orin streaming exists but USB/host timestamps of the two boards are not sample-accurate; all sync must be in-band (the electrical pulse), never from host timestamps.

The GPU is not needed for dechirp at BW 4-8 kHz (CPU can do it); the honest GPU story is the batched 4-channel bin-profile correlation, SRP-PHAT/GCC grids at 96 kHz, the learned demod, and running Whisper concurrently, all under a measured power budget. Do not oversell 'GPU demodulation'.

Aberdeen local flavour: cite Sherlock 8084730 (OCEANS 2017 Aberdeen) and frame the pool as harbour/structure-inspection confined water.

evidence: Reverberation-aware dechirp is pre-empted: Xie, Zhang, You, Wang, Wang, Fu, 'Combating Multi-Path Interference to Improve Chirp-based Underwater Acoustic Communication' (UWLoRa+), IEEE arnumber 10623112 (2024), arXiv 2311.17624. LoRa-style FSCM (22-28 kHz, BW 6 kHz, SF 8) in an INDOOR SWIMMING POOL (4.6 x 3.0 x 1.5 m) with 'amplitude of other paths may be larger than the first path'. They detect every path from the PREAMBLE (sliding-window cross-correlation, oversampled), dechirp+FFT each time-aligned path window, and combine the per-path peak amplitudes ('add the amplitudes of these path windows with the same data, and retain the maximal peak') - i.e. a preamble-trained multipath-diversity combiner in the dechirp domain, plus non-linear chirps and NB-LDPC. 3x BER improvement vs LoRa. The proposal's 'bin-profile h[b] circular cross-correlation' is the same idea expressed as one FFT-domain matched filter; it is a reformulation, not a new receiver.

Same idea, older, in the corpus: 'Chirp spread spectrum of OFDM UWA communication based on multi-path diversity receive' (ResearchGate 279017920); VTRM (virtual time-reversal mirror) CSS receivers 9990102 (IBCAST 2022) and 'M-ary nonlinear sine chirp spread spectrum ... virtual time-reversal mirror' (EURASIP JWCN 2021, s13638-021-01995-3) - preamble/probe-estimated channel used as a matched filter for chirp symbols in multipath. Also 11130177 (JOE 2025, virtual time compressed mirror sparse equaliser).

Consumer speaker as underwater chirp transmitter in a pool, received by distributed hydrophones, multipath-aware, with TDOA localisation from the chirp itself and NO TX-RX clock sync: Yang & Zheng, 'AquaHelper: Underwater SOS Transmission and Detection in Swimming Pools', ACM SenSys 2023, DOI 10.1145/3625687.3625816. Smartwatch speaker, 1.5-3.5 kHz linear chirp, dechirp+FFT detection, coherent combining of harmonics / windows / MULTIPLE SPATIAL RECEIVERS, earliest-peak direct-path selection against wall reflections, pairwise sample-level sync with pool-geometry TDOA bounds, grid likelihood map of swimmer position. Carries no payload, receivers are pool-wall fixed - but 'chirp from consumer speaker + hydrophones + pool reverberation + TDOA position from the same chirp' is done.

Consumer-device underwater PHY and ranging are established: Chen, Chan, Gollakota 'Underwater Messaging Using Mobile Devices' SIGCOMM 2022 (10.1145/3544216.3544258), 'Underwater Acoustic Ranging Between Smartphones' (arXiv 2209.01780, dual-mic direct-path identification under severe multipath, works with clock drift, 0.48-0.86 m median to 35 m), 'Underwater 3D positioning on smart devices' SIGCOMM 2023 (10.1145/3603269.3604851).

'Comm packet doubles as localisation signal' with CSS: Rezzouki et al. 9706010 (OCEANS 2021, DCSS comm + localisation) and 10618907 (IEEE 2024, 'Sustainable Fishing: Chirp-Based Signals for UAC and Localization' - DCSS data link + MULTIPLE SYNCHRONISED HYDROPHONES computing TDOA to localise the transmitter; ocean BER experiments + Bellhop RMSE). Also Renner/Heitmann/Steinmetz 'ahoi' (ACM TOSN 2020, 10.1145/3376921): inexpensive modem doing communication AND localisation for micro-AUVs.

Commodity-hardware CSS + learned demod in confined/shallow water: DeWater 11571741 (INFOCOM 2026) already benchmarks dechirp vs learned demod in pond/lake/river with a vibration-motor transmitter; their related-work section explicitly cites AquaHelper and AquaApp, so reviewers from that community will know all of the above.

Underwater LoRa receiver design (sync, STO/SFO, Doppler) is mature: Steinmetz & Renner 9905674 (UComms 2022), 10322772 (IEEE Access 2023, Doppler+SFO robust sync), WUWNet 2023 differential FSCM (10.1145/3631726.3631740), UComms 2024 SSC vs FSCM in shallow water; Petroni 10283587 / 11644049; 11232417 (fc/SF trade-offs). Nothing in the proposed TX/RX chain beyond the combiner is new.

What was NOT found in ~390-record corpus, 3 IEEE searches, and web: (i) a CSS/LoRa data link received on an AUV-mounted multi-element hydrophone array with real-time on-vehicle GPU decode and measured latency/power; (ii) per-packet bearing from the LoRa preamble on a vehicle array with two unsynchronised ADC boards; (iii) a head-to-head of UWLoRa+-style path combining vs bin-profile matched filter vs DeWater-style learned demod under controlled, ground-truthed delay spread. These are systems/evaluation contributions, not algorithmic firsts.

Reframe P2 as a systems + controlled-evaluation paper: 'Real-time LoRa-style CSS reception on an AUV hydrophone array with an embedded GPU: a ground-truthed pool study of delay-spread-limited decoding'. votes.lens: Feasibility / pool-test engineering (3 people, 25 m reverberant concrete pool, consumer SD speaker, 4 hydrophones on two unsynchronised Daisy boards over USB CDC, Jetson AGX Orin)
evidence: Novelty of the comms half is already taken: AquaHelper (Yang & Zheng, ACM SenSys 2023, 'Underwater SOS transmission and detection in swimming pools') is commodity-device CSS in a swimming pool and is cited by DeWater (11571741) as ref [23]; AquaApp (Chen/Chan/Gollakota, SIGCOMM 2022) already transmits from consumer speakers underwater; DeWater (INFOCOM 2026) is commodity TX + learned CSS demod. The proposal cites none of AquaHelper and only narrows around AquaApp.

The reverberation-aware decoder may have no gap to close at the proposed operating point: Steinmetz 9905674 shows that once Tsym exceeds the multipath spread (SF>=8 in CASTLE-2, 5 ms multipath = 100 bins at BW 20 kHz) plain dechirp already syncs 100% and gives BER <2%; in his 190 m canal trial all SFs synced 100% at ~26 dB SNR and the dominant residual error was fractional STO splitting energy across two bins plus channel variation over long packets, not echoes. At SF 8-9 / BW 4 kHz (64-128 ms symbols) with a ~30 ms pool tail (Sabine estimate RT60 ~95 ms, T20 ~30 ms for 25x12x2 m concrete) and the direct path strongest, plain argmax will likely land at low single-digit SER, leaving the headline contribution with a small, noisy effect to demonstrate.

The bin-profile model is only exact for the in-window part of each echo; the previous-symbol leak is tau/Tsym (~23% at SF9/4 kHz for a 30 ms echo, ~47% at SF8/4 kHz), is symbol-dependent, and is baked into h[b] estimated from the all-zero preamble. This is a modelling error in the proposed 'matched-filter gain' claim unless decision feedback on the previous symbol is added.

Cross-board TDOA hardware does not exist: two Daisy Seed crystals drift ~30 ppm -> ~4.4 cm/s of path-difference drift; the proposal's own fix (electrical sync burst summed into channel 1 of both boards) is an unbuilt analog mod on the hydrophone front end that must be designed, soldered, and validated before pool session 1, competing with P1 for the same September window. The README (research/eli/README.md) and 00_directions.md list it as an unsolved hazard, and the 'nuisance parameter' fallback is underdetermined per packet (3 TDOAs vs 3 coords + offset) as the proposal itself admits.

The existing capture path is not sample-accurate: gen2/daisyseed_firmware/stream_audio.cpp drops newest samples when the host stalls ('host not draining - drop newest samples'), uses an 8-bit seq (a stall >85 ms at 96 kHz is ambiguous), and research/whisper_ivc/daisy_stream.py documents that the cdc-acm throttle path 'loses AND reorders chunks (seen as seq jumping forward then backward)'; the daisyseed README calls the Orin's USB hub 'marginal' with -71/-110 errors. The stack was built for 16 kHz Whisper; any drop inside a CSS frame is a sync loss and any drop between sync pulses corrupts cross-board timing. This must be re-engineered and drop-tested at 2x96 kHz/24-bit before any TDOA or real-time decode claim.

No hydrophone geometry is documented anywhere in the repo (grep over README.md, gen2/, misc/hydrophone_plot); the bearing claim from two same-board pairs requires the two pairs to be non-collinear. If the wiring is front-pair on one board and back-pair on the other, the two cones are near-parallel and the intersection is ill-conditioned; this is unknown today.

Lloyd's mirror geometry: sub on the bottom (hydrophones ~1.7 m deep) and speaker at 1 m gives surface-path excess delay 0.65 ms at 3 m, 0.23 ms at 10 m, 0.11 ms at 20 m, versus a GCC-PHAT main-lobe width of 1/BW = 0.25 ms at 4 kHz (0.125 ms at 8 kHz). Direct and surface arrivals are unresolvable for most of the pool, so only azimuth bearing is defensible; elevation, range-from-arrival-structure, and 'position error in m' claims beyond a single cone intersection are not.

Learned-demod baseline: DeWater trained on 32,000 symbols per scenario plus 50,000 pretrain symbols on an RTX 3090 with 5-fold CV inside each site. The plan's ~2,000 symbols x 30 poses (~60k) is sufficient in count only if the per-pose files actually contain that many symbols: 6 frames x 4 SFs x ~32 data symbols is ~800 symbols per 90 s file, not 2,000, and at SF9/4 kHz a single 32-symbol frame is ~5.4 s, so a 90 s file cannot hold 6 frames at each of four SFs plus a pilot. The pose budget or the symbol count per pose has to shrink, which cuts training data below the DeWater regime.

Speaker band assumption (fc 9-10 kHz, BW 4-8 kHz) is unverified; consumer SD-card 'pool speakers' are dynamic drivers in sealed plastic shells whose underwater output above ~6-8 kHz typically collapses. If the usable BW is 2 kHz, SF9 symbols become 256 ms (35 bit/s), GCC-PHAT lobe width doubles to 0.5 ms, and the Lloyd's-mirror overlap worsens. The Week-1 sweep is correctly planned but the whole SF/BW table and the bearing precision argument hinge on it.

Whisper-over-audio WER vs text-over-CSS CER (Rong 11104740) is not a like-for-like metric and the existing IVC has no reported baseline WER in the pool; it is a fine application paragraph but cannot carry the paper.

direction.name: Open 4-channel pool hydrophone dataset with labelled source poses + sim2real gap study for DL DOA

proposal.one_line_claim: First public raw 4-channel 96 kHz hydrophone-array recordings from a small AUV in a bounded reverberant pool with ~100 labelled source poses, plus a controlled sim2real study quantifying how much of the DL-DOA degradation is due to wall reverberation vs hull/array-manifold error vs source response vs clock error, and how many real poses it takes to close the gap.
proposal.method: Data pipeline (Monday-ready): (1) Probe file on the speaker's SD card, WAV not MP3: a 1 s 1-18 kHz LFM sync sweep, then 30 x {4 ms CW ping at 5/8/12/16 kHz at 1 Hz (audio-band stand-in for a RoboSub pinger), 50 ms LFM 2-18 kHz, 2 s exponential sine sweep for impulse-response extraction}, ~60 s per pose. A subset of poses adds speech and DeepShip clips. (2) Orin records both Daisy streams losslessly with per-buffer sequence counters (dropped samples silently destroy TDOA). (3) Per-pose label = speaker xyz + speaker yaw (it is directional), array xyz + sub yaw, water temperature -> c, thruster state, session id. Sim side: pyroomacoustics ShoeBox with c=1480 m/s, measured pool dims, surface reflection -1, concrete walls |R|~0.9, image-source order 6-10, array at the measured geometry, source = measured speaker response (from a 1 m hydrophone recording) convolved in. Generate 3 training sets: FF (free field + noise, i.e. the Song 2025 recipe), ISM (shoebox), ISM+ (shoebox + measured speaker response + hull-manifold calibration from 5 real poses). Estimator under test: 6 pair-wise STFT phase-difference maps (Song 2025 input) -> small CNN -> (sin az, cos az, el) regression, ~1M params, exported to TensorRT on the Orin. Also a second learned model on GCC-PHAT vectors from the 6 pairs (SELDnet-lite). Study: train on FF/ISM/ISM+, evaluate on real; then fine-tune with N=5,10,20,40 real poses; ablate which sim ingredient (walls, speaker response, manifold, clock jitter injected as +/-k samples on cross-board pairs) moves the real-data MAE. Output: dataset (raw WAV + JSON labels + loader + baselines, released with the paper) and the gap curves.
proposal.experiment_plan: Pool sessions (3 people: recorder/Orin, pole mover, pose logger). Session 0 (bench, ~half day): validate two-board sync by feeding one electrical click into both boards and confirming constant sample offset; verify SD playback is uncompressed and start-time jitter is handled by the sync sweep. Session 1 (~3 h): array static at mid-pool, depth ~1 m; speaker on a rigid marked pole at 8 azimuths x 3 ranges (2, 5, 10 m) x 2 depths = 48 poses, 60 s probe each, plus a 1 m speaker-response recording at the start. Session 2 (~3 h): array moved next to a wall/corner (worst-case reverberation), thrusters on/off subset, speech/DeepShip subset, ~40 poses. Session 3 (different day, ~3 h): held-out evaluation set at new poses and a different sub yaw, ~40 poses; optional control subset with the 4 hydrophones on a bare frame off the hull to isolate manifold error. Ground truth: pool tile/lane grid + tape from two walls + depth marks on the pole + plumb line; topside camera with an AprilTag on the pole above water as a cross-check; expected 3-5 cm, i.e. <1.5 deg at 2 m and <0.3 deg at 10 m; log water temperature for c. Total ~130 poses. Baselines: GCC-PHAT + least-squares DOA, SRP-PHAT grid, broadband incoherent MUSIC, Takada-2019-style multipath peak rejection, and the Song 2025 network trained free-field. Metrics: azimuth/elevation MAE and median, miss-detection rate (>15 deg), per-region breakdown (centre vs near-wall), MAE vs number of real fine-tuning poses, MAE vs injected cross-board clock error, Orin latency and power (jtop) per estimator.

hardware_blockers: Two Daisy Seed boards with independent crystals: ~20-50 ppm relative drift = 2-5 samples/s at 96 kHz, while the full cross-board TDOA on a ~0.3 m baseline is only ~19 samples; uncorrected, cross-board pairs are useless within seconds. Preferred fix: make board B's SAI/codec a clock slave to board A's MCLK/BCLK/LRCLK over three wires (STM32H7 SAI supports slave mode), then resolve the residual integer-sample DMA start offset once per session with a shared electrical click. Fallback: board A GPIO pulse train timestamped by both boards' sample counters, plus piecewise-linear resampling. Must be verified on the bench before any pool time; without it the dataset only has 2 truly synchronous pairs, which is not enough for 3D DOA.

Speaker band <= ~20 kHz: cannot emit RoboSub 25-40 kHz pinger tones, so the 'pinger' claim must be worded as audio-band beacon; at 10 kHz lambda = 15 cm so a 0.3 m baseline is > lambda/2 and narrowband CW pings are phase-ambiguous (broadband chirps resolve it). Response, directivity and THD are unknown: record a 1 m response at the start of every session, log speaker yaw as a label, confirm the SD player outputs uncompressed WAV and does not resample or apply DSP.

SD-card playback start-time jitter and possible clock offset of the player: every pose recording needs the in-band sync sweep; no absolute time-of-flight is available (no range from TOA), only TDOA-based DOA.
Lossless capture on the Orin: dropped USB/serial buffers silently corrupt TDOA; need per-buffer sequence counters from the Daisy firmware and a drop detector before the pool session.

Ground-truth rig: rigid marked pole for the speaker, plumb line, tape from two walls, tile grid, topside camera + AprilTag; sub position measured once per placement; expect 3-5 cm which is fine for DOA labels but marginal if range/3D position labels are claimed.

Array geometry and hull scattering: hydrophone positions on the sub must be measured to ~5 mm; the hull perturbs the manifold, which is part of the sim2real gap; an off-hull bare-frame control subset is needed to separate it.

Pool logistics: pump/filtration noise and lane-swimmer noise vary by time; water temperature (c changes ~3 m/s per degC) must be logged; 3-hour sessions with 3 people cap throughput at ~45-50 poses per session.
proposal.track: Track 02 Sonar Signal/Image Processing & Communication (array processing / DL-DOA benchmark), submitted in parallel to the Student Poster Competition; Track 01 Underwater Acoustics is the fallback if the paper leans toward pool propagation/calibration.

evidence: Woodward, Reiss & Magnasco 2020, PLOS ONE 15(6):e0235155, 'Learning to localize sounds in a highly reverberant environment: Machine-learning tracking of dolphin whistle-like sounds in a pool': 16 hydrophones (four 4-element sub-arrays), 192 kHz, 33.5 m half-cylindrical concrete aquarium pool, synthetic whistles played from speakers at 14 laser-rangefinder-surveyed positions (7 xy x 2 depths), TDOA + normalized cross-correlation features -> RF/SVM/GPR, GPR beats SRP (0.66 m median error), data public at figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7956212. This directly kills the 'first public multichannel hydrophone recordings in a bounded reverberant pool with ground-truth source positions + ML localization' wording.

Yi Lu 2024, IEEE DataPort doi:10.21227/2mh4-4r49, 'underwater common wideband sound source 6-element circular array received dataset': 6-element circular array (r=4.6 cm), chirps/QPSK/multitone/OFDM, array rotated 0-330 deg in 30 deg steps at 4 m and 19 m in a tank (anechoic), 24 sets, released with a paper (doi:10.1007/s11277-025-11759-7). A public tank array-DOA dataset with angle labels already exists; yours would not be the first.

Srivastava, Deleforge et al. 2023 (JASA) 'How to (virtually) train your sound source localizer' and Neural-SRP (arXiv 2403.09455): the exact proposed ablation -- ISM shoebox realism controlled per ingredient (wall absorption, source directivity, receiver response), simulated-vs-measured RIR training, fine-tuning with ~250 real samples -- is an established air-acoustics recipe; LOCATA (Zenodo 3630471) is the reference public multichannel DOA benchmark. The sim2real-gap-by-ingredient study is a port, not a new methodology.

IEEE 11616801 Yan 2026 (OCEANS Sanya) pretrain-on-sim / fine-tune-on-few-measured underwater source localization with contrastive loss, and IEEE 10891008 Zhang 2025 (SPL) limited-data underwater DOA: the pretrain-sim/fine-tune-real curve is already published in the underwater domain, so 'how many real poses close the gap' is incremental.

IEEE 8096292 Kasetkasem 2017: 4-hydrophone array, 192 kHz, pinger moved to 5 surveyed positions in Kasetsart University diving pool, multipath-aware DOA -- prior pool-array-pinger-DOA exists (no release).

RGU Aberdeen (host institution of OCEANS 2027) MetroSea 2025 paper 'Deep learning-based DOA estimation for underwater acoustic sources' (rgu-repository worktribe 3168713): CNN DOA on 8-element linear/circular arrays, 15/20 kHz BPSK sources, simulated multipath only, 2.5-4.2 deg RMSE -- local reviewers will know DL-DOA-on-sim is commodity; only real-data evidence distinguishes you.

Corpus check (393 IEEE records in the search corpus): no AUV-hull-mounted compact-array pool dataset with pose labels; 3 permitted ieee.py searches returned 0 hits (tool/query issue, treat as inconclusive).
votes.fix: Drop 'first public pool hydrophone dataset' and 'sim2real gap study' as the headline; both have prior art (Woodward 2020 pool dataset with 14 GT positions on figshare; Lu 2024 tank array-DOA dataset; Srivastava 2023 ingredient ablation in air; Yan 2026 sim-pretrain/real-finetune underwater). What survives is narrower and vehicle-specific: 'first public dataset and gap attribution for a compact (4-element, ~0.3 m) hydrophone array mounted on an AUV hull in a reverberant pool, isolating the vehicle-borne error sources that have no air-acoustics or fixed-infrastructure analogue: hull-perturbed array manifold (bare-frame control), thruster self-noise on/off, and cross-board sample-clock error, with on-vehicle Jetson Orin latency/power for every estimator.' Cite Woodward 2020 and Lu 2024 explicitly as the existing datasets and position yours as the mobile-platform complement (they are fixed 16-element infrastructure / anechoic tank, classification over 14 positions / 12 angles; you give ~130 poses, planar hull array, regression, broadband probe + speech/DeepShip, edge deployment). Keep the ablation but cite Srivastava/Neural-SRP as the recipe being ported and make the contribution the finding (which ingredient dominates for a hull array in a 25 m concrete pool), not the method. Best fit: Student Poster Competition or a companion dataset paper to P1, not the headline OCEANS paper.

votes.lens: Feasibility / pool-test engineering (ground truth, sync, capture chain, pose budget, claim scope)
evidence: 'First public multichannel hydrophone-array dataset with ground-truth source positions' is false as worded: SWellEx-96 (1996, public, 21-el VLA + HLAs, GPS-tracked towed source) and several ONR sea-trial datasets already exist; LOCATA (air) is the methodological standard reviewers will hold a DOA dataset to. Only 'AUV-mounted compact array in a bounded reverberant pool' is defensible. Corpus check: no IEEE record in the 393-record set releases a pool/tank array dataset (only 10244416 SSS sim and 11226529 timbre transfer mention data release), so the narrowed claim holds.

Elevation labels/estimation cannot be validated in this pool: at range 5-10 m with array at ~1 m depth in a ~1.5-2.5 m deep pool, elevation to a source spans only a few degrees, the planar hull array has an up/down mirror ambiguity, and the surface image (R=-1) arrives ~10-15 samples (at 96 kHz) after the direct path at 10 m, i.e. inside one 50 ms 2-18 kHz chirp resolution cell (1/BW = 6 samples) and fully overlapping a 4 ms CW ping (Lloyd's mirror nulls). 3-5 cm pose error is fine for azimuth but elevation MAE numbers would be noise. Kasetkasem 2017 (8096292) with a 4-element square array in a university pool reports 5-13 deg azimuth errors and 'accurate for small elevation only' at 5 poses with no stated ground-truth accuracy.

Pose budget vs claim: 8 azimuths x 3 ranges x 2 depths = 45 deg azimuth spacing. Evaluating at a different sub yaw puts test azimuths up to 22 deg from any real training azimuth, so the 'MAE vs N real fine-tuning poses' curve conflates CNN interpolation failure with sim2real gap (Song 2025, 11104616, explicitly reports errors blow up outside the trained azimuth range, 6.29 deg at 27 deg vs ~1 deg on-axis, with only 20 lake azimuths). Closing that needs <=10-15 deg spacing = 24-36 azimuths per ring; with realistic 2-3 min per pose (move pole, settle, log, 20-60 s probe) a 3 h session yields ~45-60 poses, so the 3-range x 2-depth factorial does not fit in 3 sessions alongside a held-out set.

Proposal's preferred sync fix does not exist on this hardware: Daisy Seed's onboard codec hangs off SAI1 with MCLK/BCLK/LRCLK routed internally (not on header pins); only SAI2 is exposed, so 'make board B a clock slave over three wires' requires an external codec board. Only the GPIO-pulse-timestamped-by-sample-counter fallback + resampling is doable with what is on the bench. Drift estimate is right: crystal ~20-50 ppm relative -> 2-5 samples/s vs ~19-sample full cross-board TDOA on a 0.3 m baseline.

Capture chain is currently lossy and silently so: gen2/daisyseed_firmware/stream_audio.cpp AudioCallback drops newest samples on ring overflow with no marker (the u8 seq is per 64-sample frame and only advances for frames actually sent), so ring drops cannot be detected on the host; research/whisper_ivc/daisy_stream.py docstring says the Orin cdc-acm path 'loses AND reorders chunks' and needed a cat-pipe workaround; the firmware README documents flaky Orin USB enumeration (-71/-110 errors, garbled serials). 96 kHz/24-bit x2 boards = ~1.15 MB/s over two CDC links. A 32-bit sample counter in every frame and a drop-aware recorder must be written before session 0 counts.

Ground-truth logistics not addressed: a 25 m pool is ~10-12.5 m wide, so an array at mid-pool is >=5 m from any deck edge; the 2 m and 5 m rings need a person in the water holding a pole (cannot hold 3-5 cm; a body is a strong scatterer; safety) or a floating/bottom rig. Sub yaw for a neutrally buoyant vehicle at 1 m depth over 3 h is not 'measured once per placement'; a 2 deg heading drift exceeds the claimed label accuracy. Li & Chitre 2023 (10224658) needed a fishing-line/reel/sliding-block rig and 40 s averaging to get ~4 cm and still reported 'small-scale oscillations' corrupting phase in a 2.5 m tank; they call the tank 'surprisingly complicated to model' with 'strong sensitivity to minor geometrical irregularities of the tank wall' - i.e. the ISM shoebox will be far off, which is fine for the ablation but rules out using ISM as a label check.

Speaker unknowns are unverified: cheap TF-card underwater speakers are typically MP3 players with 16 kHz low-pass, auto-gain and stereo-to-mono; 'WAV not MP3' is an assumption, not a fact. Not fatal (the 1 m response recording captures whatever it does) but the 'exponential sine sweep for IR extraction' and 16 kHz CW ping may not survive.

What is NOT a blocker: Orin TensorRT latency/power for a ~1M-param CNN is trivial; sim data is unlimited; a pool dataset + sim2real ablation is an accepted OCEANS/student-poster paper shape (11244929 Huynh 2025 got in with exactly that framing for Ping360). Abstract by 7 Dec 2026 is reachable if session 1 happens by mid-Nov and only the GPIO sync fallback is attempted.
votes.fix: Narrow to a 2D azimuth-only, single-depth dataset and ablation: (1) Claim: 'first public AUV-hull compact-array recordings in a bounded reverberant pool with labelled source azimuth/range', cite SWellEx-96/LOCATA as the sea/air precedents; drop elevation and 3D DOA entirely (report elevation only as a documented limitation), keep range as a coarse label. (2) Geometry: clamp the sub to the bottom or a frame near a deck edge/corner (which is also the reverberant case you wanted) with a surface mast + AprilTag for yaw to <0.5 deg; source on a weighted floor stand or a lane-rope-guided float at marked tile positions, all within pole reach of the deck. (3) Pose plan: two azimuth rings at 2 m and 4-5 m with 10-15 deg spacing (~50-60 poses) in session 1, 20-30 s probe per pose (10 reps, not 30), thruster on/off + speech/DeepShip subset in session 2, and a held-out session 3 with the SAME azimuth grid at a rotated sub yaw so interpolation vs sim2real is separable (train/test interleaved azimuths as a control). (4) Sync: abandon the SAI-slave idea; master GPIO 1 Hz pulse into slave EXTI, both boards stamp a 32-bit sample counter into every USB frame, host detects drops and piecewise-linear resamples; verify on the bench with an electrical click and report residual cross-board TDOA std as a dataset spec. Fix the silent ring-overflow drop in stream_audio.cpp first. (5) Study: keep the sim-ingredient ablation (walls / measured speaker response / hull manifold / injected clock error) as the headline result and demote the N-pose fine-tuning curve to a secondary figure. (6) Verify speaker WAV/AGC behaviour with an oscilloscope on the driver before designing the probe file. Submit to Student Poster + Track 02; this narrowed version fits 3 sessions and 3 people.

direction.name: Thruster-telemetry-conditioned multichannel Noise2Noise self-noise denoiser on the Orin

proposal.one_line_claim: A thruster-telemetry-conditioned, lightweight multichannel self-noise suppressor for a 4-hydrophone AUV array, trained only from the vehicle's own thruster-only and thruster-off pool recordings (no simulator, no clean labels, no reference accelerometer), running in real time on the on-board Jetson AGX Orin and measurably restoring GCC-PHAT bearing, chirp detection, and Whisper WER under thruster noise.
proposal.method:
Key correction to the D4 sketch: thruster noise is NOT decorrelated across channels (thrusters are fixed near-field sources), so WaveN2N-style cross-channel Noise2Noise will *preserve* it as "signal". What separates ego-noise from targets is (a) telemetry that predicts it and (b) fixed vehicle-relative geometry. So the recipe is telemetry-conditioned, self-labelled from the vehicle's own recordings, not pure N2N.

Data: (1) thruster-only recordings N(t) with time-aligned PWM commands (ESC RPM if BLHeli telemetry exists) and IMU at >=50 Hz; (2) thruster-off recordings S(t) of the speaker at gridded poses. Training pairs are real-through-real mixtures S + a*N at random SNR (-15..+15 dB), with N's telemetry as the conditioning vector c(t). Optional true-N2N term: repeated identical PWM scripts give two noise realizations sharing c(t); same-board channel pairs give decorrelated electronic/flow components.

Model (target <1 M params, TensorRT FP16): STFT (1024/256 @96 kHz) of a same-board 2-ch pair (avoids the clock issue); c(t) enters via FiLM into a 2-layer GRU mask network (DTLN/DeepFilterNet-lite) predicting per-channel complex ratio masks. A DDSP branch synthesizes a noise reference: per thruster, harmonic oscillators at f0 = k*RPM (blade-pass and pole-pair harmonics) plus filtered noise with learned per-channel transfer filters; its output is an extra input channel and also serves as the reference for a classical NLMS baseline. Loss: multi-res STFT + SI-SDR on the thruster-off target (reverb deliberately retained, since P1 exploits echoes) + a GCC-PHAT consistency term so inter-channel phase survives for TDOA. Outputs: denoised 4-ch waveform at 96 kHz, ~11 ms hop latency. Ablations: no conditioning / PWM only / PWM+IMU / DDSP reference only / full.
proposal.experiment_plan: Session 1 (~3 h, 3 people: thruster driver+logger, speaker mover, Orin operator). Sub clamped to a weighted frame at pool centre, hydrophones ~1 m deep. (a) Thruster-only: each thruster stepped 0-100% in 10% steps x 10 s, both directions; 20 min random-walk PWM on all thrusters; one fixed 5-min PWM script recorded twice (N2N pairs). Check ADC gain for clipping first. (b) Thrusters off: speaker at ~10 poses (2-20 m, several bearings; tape-measure + lane markers, +-10 cm is enough) playing one 10-min SD file: 1-18 kHz log chirps, 10 ms CW pulses at 5/10/15 kHz (pinger-like), CSS frames from P2, ~3 min speech, silence, with a loud sync chirp at file start for alignment. (c) Real held-out: same file while thrusters run scripted profiles at 3 poses. Session 2 (~3 h): 5 new poses with thrusters on, plus free-swimming runs where telemetry varies naturally (hardest, most convincing). Ground truth = the known played waveform: matched-filter detection/PSLR vs chirps, GCC-PHAT TDOA on same-board pair vs the thruster-off TDOA at the same pose, transcript-based Whisper WER; SI-SDR/segmental SNR only on synthetic mixtures. Metrics: delta SI-SDR, chirp detection probability and PSLR vs thruster level, TDOA RMSE, Whisper-base/small WER vs thruster level, and Orin latency, real-time factor and power (jtop). Also report whether the conditioned model beats the PWM-indexed spectral-subtraction table on transitions and multi-thruster combos; if it does not, say so.
baselines: Spectral subtraction / Wiener with a PWM-indexed noise-PSD lookup table (the strong dumb baseline; must be beaten)
MVDR/GEV beamformer on the 2 same-board channels with noise covariance from thruster-only segments indexed by PWM
NLMS/RLS adaptive noise cancellation using the DDSP-synthesized telemetry reference (classical ANC without a physical reference sensor)
WaveN2N reimplementation (Koh 2020, 9389338): cross-channel Noise2Noise, log-Pearson loss, Wave-U-Net
Unconditioned version of our mask network (same architecture, no telemetry) to isolate the conditioning gain
Ego-noise template subtraction indexed by motor state, as in terrestrial robot audition (Ince/Nakadai 2009 style)

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: WaveN2N: Noise2Noise across hydrophone-array channels with a delay/scale-invariant log-Pearson loss on a Wave-U-Net; 8-element VLA sea data at 10 kHz; removes ambient noise AND reverberation; assumes noise decorrelated across channels; offline, single-channel inference.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Our dominant noise (thrusters) is spatially coherent, violating their core assumption; we add telemetry conditioning and a DDSP noise-reference branch, deliberately preserve reverberation and inter-channel phase (TDOA/P1 need them), train from the vehicle's own thruster-only/thruster-off recordings, and run in real time on the Orin with downstream task metrics.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Deep-learning wide-band self-noise suppression for an underwater glider with integrated hydrophones (USYS 2024, 0 cites; abstract only in corpus, must fetch full text).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Glider has no propeller and no fast-varying actuation; they appear to use no vehicle telemetry, single channel, offline. We target propeller-driven thruster noise that tracks PWM/RPM, use telemetry as side information, multichannel, on-vehicle real time.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Fiber-optic hydrophone with an embedded reference sensor whose signal is used as side information for DL denoising of sensor phase noise.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Same idea of a reference/side channel for DL denoising, but their noise is sensor-intrinsic and needs extra hardware; our reference is free vehicle telemetry (commands already on the bus) and the noise is acoustic ego-noise.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Resource-efficient speech enhancement on wearables using a DDSP vocoder refinement stage (ASRU 2025).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: We borrow the light DDSP-on-edge design pattern but invert it: DDSP synthesizes the *noise* (harmonics locked to RPM) rather than the speech, and the domain is hydrophones at 96 kHz on a Jetson.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Saliency ConvLSTM DOA on a 3-hydrophone array for compact vehicles; explicitly lists 'integrate inertial sensor data into the model input' as future work.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: We do exactly the telemetry/IMU fusion they defer, but as a front-end denoiser that improves classical GCC-PHAT rather than a new DOA net; we also report edge latency, which they do not.

closest_prior_work.first_author: Ince / Schmidt / Wang-Cavallaro (robot & drone ego-noise literature)
closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Terrestrial robot audition: ego-noise suppression using motor-state templates (Ince, Nakadai et al., IROS 2009), motor-data-guided dictionaries (Schmidt, Loellmann, Kellermann, IWAENC 2014), and multi-rotor drone ego-noise reduction from motor speed (Wang & Cavallaro, AVSS 2016 / IEEE Sensors J 2018).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: This is the real intellectual ancestor and a reviewer from robot audition will expect it cited. Novelty here is the underwater port: hydrophone array on a propeller AUV in a reverberant tank, learned rather than template-based, self-labelled from thruster-off/thruster-on pool recordings, evaluated on TDOA/chirp/WER tasks and deployed on the vehicle GPU. Not 'first use of motor telemetry for denoising'; 'first underwater/AUV one'.

hardware_blockers: Two Daisy boards, no shared clock (~+-20-50 ppm -> up to ~5 samples/s relative drift at 96 kHz): mitigated by design here (mask network runs per same-board 2-ch pair), but joint 4-ch spatial filtering and the P1 hand-off need drift correction. Options: Orin GPIO sync pulse sampled on a spare Daisy ADC pin with firmware stamping the audio sample counter at each edge; or track cross-board offset continuously by cross-correlating the (coherent, fixed-position) thruster noise itself. Must also timestamp USB audio blocks on the Orin so PWM/IMU logs align to audio to within ~1 block (~10 ms is fine, PWM is slow).

Telemetry access: need PWM commands logged at >=50 Hz with Orin timestamps; ESC RPM telemetry (BLHeli32 serial) would be much better than commanded PWM (load-dependent lag); check whether the ESCs expose it. Without RPM, harmonic tracking in the DDSP branch is approximate.

Speaker band <=20 kHz and uncalibrated: all evaluation signals limited to ~1-18 kHz, so nothing is shown for the 25-40 kHz RoboSub pinger band; thruster noise is strongest below ~10 kHz so the core claim is unaffected, but the RoboSub tie-in needs a real pinger (~$100-300 or piezo + amp). Unknown SPL means physical SNR is set by distance/thruster level; controlled SNR sweeps must be synthetic mixtures. SD-card playback has no trigger and its clock drifts vs ours, so alignment is via a loud sync chirp per file, not sample-exact across separate playbacks.

Vehicle must not move while thrusters run: needs a clamp/tether rig; clamped-thrust cavitation and rig vibration may differ from free-flight noise, so free-swimming eval runs in session 2 are essential and are where the method could fail.
ADC front-end clipping: thruster noise at the hydrophones is far louder than a distant speaker; check gain/24-bit headroom before session 1 or the dataset is useless.
Structure-borne vs waterborne self-noise depends on hydrophone mounting; if mostly structure-borne, mounting changes could invalidate a trained model (report mounting explicitly).

Risk that a PWM-indexed spectral-subtraction table matches the learned model on steady thrust: the paper's contribution then rests on transitions/combos and on the downstream-task + Orin numbers; plan the eval to expose this rather than hide it.
