evidence: IEEE 10103424 (Underwater Technology 2023, Tokyo): 'Self-Noise Suppression for AUV without Clean Data: a Noise2Noise Approach' -- self-supervised N2N AUV self-noise suppression from single-hydrophone data, real South China Sea AUV recordings. Kills the 'trained only from the vehicle's own recordings, no clean labels' claim; the directions note (which says 'no self-noise cancellation conditioned on thruster telemetry') missed this paper because it is not in the 393-record corpus.

Wang, Tian, Li, Sun, Yu, JASA 2026 (PubMed 41528165): 'Motion-aware sonar denoising for AUV self-noise using a speed-conditioned U-Net-transformer dual-branch cGAN' (Speed-UT2-CGAN). Vehicle SPEED telemetry is fed as a conditioning input; trained on synthetic mixtures of REAL AUV self-noise from lake trials + ShipsEar at controlled SNR; multi-res time+frequency losses; compared against classical, SEGAN and DPRNN baselines. This is the same recipe as D4 (real-through-real mixtures, telemetry conditioning) already published underwater, so 'nobody uses vehicle telemetry as side-info' is false.

Gulli, Fontana, Drioli, Salvati, Ferrin et al., EURASIP J. Audio Speech Music Process. 2025 (10.1186/s13636-025-00425-2): 'Enhancing drone audition with rotor-conditioned deep models' -- rotor-speed time series as conditioning into Wave-U-Net, DCCRN, DCUNet with three fusion strategies, ablations vs unconditioned, lightweight 25%-param variant, real ego-noise recorded with stepwise rotor speeds (36-84 RPS), SNR/SI-SDR/STOI/PESQ. Nearly the exact model-side contribution (per-motor RPM conditioning of a lightweight mask network + ablation) in air; also lists earlier motor-data-guided work: Schmidt et al. 2016 (motor-data-guided multichannel dictionary), Yen & Hioka 2018 (PSD from rotor speeds), Yen, Hioka, Schmid, Mace 2022, Manamperi et al. 2023 (GMM Wiener guided by rotor profiles).

Zhao, Xu, Xie, Ren, Wang, Yan, JASA 159(3):1749, 2026 (PubMed 41770004): 'Propeller self-noise suppression algorithm for UUVs based on a two-stage denoising-inpainting framework' -- mask-based denoising net + spectrum inpainting with a Shaft-Frequency Suppression Loss targeting propeller harmonics, trained on ShipsEar + collected UUV self-noise; reports downstream target-recognition gain. Covers the 'harmonics locked to shaft frequency' angle without needing RPM.

Ocean Engineering 2023 (S002980182302382X): 'Adaptive noise cancelling for an AUV-mounted passive inverted USBL array' -- ANC for thruster-motor/shell-vibration noise with no secondary reference sensor, explicitly shown to improve array beamforming/bearing. Pre-empts the 'classical ANC without physical reference sensor improves bearing' baseline story.

JMSE 11(7):1358, 2023: 'Self-Interference Suppression of UUV with Vector Hydrophone Array Based on an Improved Autoencoder' -- multichannel (vector array) learned self-noise suppression on a UUV; ResearchGate 392462578 (2025): 'AUV Self-noise Suppression Technique Based on Informer' -- predict-and-subtract self-noise from the vehicle's own history. Together with 10103424 these make 'multichannel, learned, self-labelled AUV self-noise suppression' a crowded 2023-2026 line, mostly Chinese groups.

IEEE 10827319 (2024) DL active noise cancellation for UAV propeller sound; IEEE 10694014 (2024) monaural speech enhancement on drone via adapter transfer learning; arXiv 2303.00829 ego-noise MVDR with learned noise spatial covariance for a mobile robot -- the MVDR/GEV-with-motor-state baseline is itself published work.

Corpus check: grep of 393 IEEE abstracts for self-noise/thruster/ego-noise/telemetry returned only 9389338 (WaveN2N), 11116134 (glider), 11371588 (FOH reference sensor); the three IEEE searches surfaced 10103424 and 10694014, confirming the local survey undercounted this literature.
votes.fix: Drop 'first telemetry-conditioned / self-labelled AUV self-noise denoiser' as the headline; it is now incremental over Wang 2026 (speed-conditioned, underwater), Gulli 2025 (rotor-conditioned, air) and 10103424 (N2N, underwater). What none of them do, and what is defensible: (1) per-thruster PWM/RPM vectors on a multi-thruster vehicle with fast transients and free-swimming telemetry (all prior underwater work uses a scalar cruise speed at 0/2/3 kn, constant heading, single sensor, offline); (2) phase/TDOA-preserving multichannel output evaluated on GCC-PHAT bearing, matched-filter chirp detection and Whisper WER rather than SNR or ship-classification accuracy; (3) causal, real-time deployment on the vehicle GPU with latency/power numbers; (4) an honest comparison against a PWM-indexed spectral-subtraction table and RPM-referenced NLMS, which prior DL papers omit. Sharpest surviving statement: 'the first real-time, on-vehicle, multichannel ego-noise suppressor for a multi-thruster AUV conditioned on per-thruster commands, evaluated on downstream bearing/detection/ASR tasks in free swimming, with a study of when learned conditioning actually beats telemetry-indexed classical suppression.' That is a systems/evaluation paper, best as a section of P1 or a Student Poster entry (Track 02), not a standalone method headline. Must cite Wang 2026, Zhao 2026, 10103424, Gulli 2025, Schmidt 2016, Yen & Hioka 2018/2022, Manamperi 2023, the Ocean Eng 2023 piUSBL ANC, and JMSE 2023 vector-array autoencoder; fetch full text of Wang 2026 and 10103424 before writing the abstract. The DDSP RPM-locked harmonic noise-reference branch is the one genuinely unexplored component and could carry a 'differentiable thruster noise model fit from telemetry' framing if it measurably beats the PSD-lookup table on transients.

votes.lens: Feasibility / pool-test engineering (D4 thruster-telemetry-conditioned self-noise denoiser)
evidence: Telemetry the method conditions on does not exist on the vehicle. gen2/teensy_firmware/STABLE_firmware/STABLE_firmware.ino drives 8 thrusters with Servo.writeMicroseconds(1100-1900) (standard Blue Robotics T200 + Basic ESC, confirmed by 'T200'/'BlueRobotics' in gen2/PCBs/MLU_BreakoutV2/*.kicad_sch and DEV_firmware.ino). Basic ESC exposes no RPM/BLHeli telemetry line, and the STABLE firmware has no IMU at all (sensors: MS5837 depth, temp, humidity, pressure; grep for imu/bno/mpu/icm/gyro/accel returns nothing). The proposal's data requirement '(1) ... PWM commands (ESC RPM if BLHeli telemetry exists) and IMU at >=50 Hz' and the DDSP branch 'harmonic oscillators at f0 = k*RPM' therefore reduce to commanded PWM only; the PWM-only vs PWM+IMU ablation axis is void, and RPM-locked harmonics must be inferred from the audio itself (load-dependent lag under changing thrust).

Audio->telemetry alignment is not currently possible: the Daisy stream carries only a u8 seq counter and fmt byte per frame (research/whisper_ivc/daisy_stream.py header [0xDA][0x7A][seq][fmt]); firmware drops newest samples when the host stalls (gen2/daisyseed_firmware/stream_audio.cpp line ~109 'host not draining -- drop newest samples') and the cdc-acm path 'loses AND reorders chunks' (daisy_stream.py Stream docstring). No Orin-side timestamping of audio blocks or sample counter exists, so the ~10 ms telemetry alignment the plan assumes requires new firmware + host work before Session 1 (in addition to Teensy PWM logging with Orin timestamps, which also does not exist: telemetry is printed as ad-hoc Serial.println strings).

Sustained thruster-only stepping (8 thrusters x 11 levels x 10 s x 2 directions, plus 20 min random walk, plus 2x5 min scripts ~ 60+ min of clamped thrust) stresses exactly the subsystem the repo flags as broken: gen3/README.md says the gen2 Power_Management boards 'had heat problems' and the gen3 replacements are not yet ordered ('TODO ... Order the PCBs', last updated 2026-07-20). No clamp/tether rig exists; 8x T200 bollard thrust (~5 kgf each at 100%) on a 'weighted frame at pool centre' with 3 people is a rig-engineering job, and clamped bollard loading changes cavitation/ vibration vs free flight (the proposal admits this and says free-swim eval 'is where the method could fail').

Free-swimming eval cannot yield the headline TDOA metric: the pool has no underwater pose ground truth (no mocap, no DVL/USBL mentioned; only tape measure + lane markers for a static sub), so TDOA RMSE vs thruster-off reference is only measurable at clamped static poses. Free-swim runs reduce to chirp detection and Whisper WER; with speech from an uncalibrated <=20 kHz consumer speaker in a highly reverberant 25 m concrete pool, thruster-off baseline WER is likely already high, making WER deltas noisy with only ~3 min speech per pose.

Prior-work check: WaveN2N (9389338, Koh 2020) explicitly requires 'noise is de-correlated among different hydrophones' (Sec. III.A) and validated on an 8-element VLA at 10 kHz with ship noise/reverberation; it offers no guidance for coherent near-field ego-noise. Shi 2024 (11116134, glider self-noise DL, 0 cites) is propeller-free and abstract-only in corpus. Song 2025 (11104616) is simulation-trained DOA with Wenz/Perlin noise, no vehicle self-noise. None of the corpus papers report a propeller-AUV self-noise dataset or pitfalls, so no de-risking from literature; the real ancestors (Ince/Nakadai 2009, Schmidt 2014, Wang & Cavallaro 2016/2018) are not in the IEEE corpus and show that motor-state-indexed template/dictionary methods already work well for quasi-stationary ego-noise, which is precisely the 'strong dumb baseline' the proposal fears.

Physics favours the baseline: T200s bolted to the same frame as the hydrophones give structure-borne + near-field waterborne noise that is spatially coherent and quasi-deterministic per PWM level, so a PWM-indexed noise-PSD/Wiener table (or per-thruster template subtraction) is expected to match a <1M-param GRU on steady thrust; the learned model's only claimed edge (transitions, multi-thruster combos) is the smallest fraction of the recorded data (10 s steps are mostly steady state) and the hardest to evaluate. A headline paper whose honest outcome is 'learned ~= lookup table' is a poor bet for Track 02, and 5 weeks to first result is optimistic given the firmware/rig prerequisites above.
votes.fix: Do not make D4 the headline. Narrow it to a PWM-command-conditioned self-noise section inside P1 (or a Student Poster) with these changes: (1) drop IMU/RPM/DDSP-harmonic claims; condition only on the 8-channel commanded PWM vector already on the Teensy bus, and add a Teensy '[TELEM]' line with a monotonic counter plus Orin-side block timestamping (and a sample counter in the Daisy frame header) before any pool time; (2) treat the PWM-indexed Wiener/spectral-subtraction table and motor-state template subtraction as the primary methods and frame the learned model as an ablation ('when does learning beat the table?'), with a small clean study on transitions and 2-3-thruster combos; (3) evaluate only on the same-board 2-ch pair, clamped-static poses for TDOA, and limit thruster levels to <=50-60% in short (<=5 s) bursts with cooling gaps until gen3 power boards exist; build/verify the clamp rig and ADC headroom in a dry/bench + 30-min pool check before Session 1; (4) report free-swim runs as chirp-detection/PSLR and WER only, with explicit hydrophone mounting and structure-borne vs waterborne characterization (tap test / thruster spun in air); (5) keep the DDSP idea only if an audio-driven tonal tracker (blade-pass f0 estimated from the noise itself) is used as the reference for NLMS. As a section of P1 this gives OCEANS-acceptable 'self-noise robustness of the localizer' results with 1 extra pool hour instead of 2 dedicated sessions.

direction.name: Passive hydrophone bearing steers the Ping360 scan sector (active-sensing fusion)

proposal.one_line_claim: A 4-hydrophone passive bearing (GCC-PHAT on two clock-independent pairs) cues a Blue Robotics Ping360 to scan only a posterior-weighted sector, cutting time-to-contact and revisit period on a moving acoustic target by roughly an order of magnitude versus the standard full 360-degree sweep, demonstrated closed-loop in a reverberant pool with ground truth.
proposal.method:
Three loosely coupled modules on the Orin, all CPU-scale (be honest in the paper: this direction does not need the GPU).

1. Passive bearing (10 Hz). Ingest the existing `stream_audio.cpp` frames from both Daisy boards at 48 kHz/16-bit (fallback from 96/24 if the Orin USB hub cannot sustain ~1.15 MB/s). Compute GCC-PHAT only on intra-board pairs (H0-H1 on master, H2-H3 on slave), each of which shares a codec clock, so no cross-board sync is required. With the two pairs mounted as orthogonal baselines (rewire hydrophone cables so each board owns one diagonal of the square), tau01 gives cos(theta), tau23 gives sin(theta), atan2 gives an unambiguous azimuth. Because the speaker plays a known broadband file (2-18 kHz chirps/pink noise), use a matched filter and take the earliest correlation peak as the direct path (Kasetkasem 8096292 logic), with peak-to-sidelobe ratio as confidence. Output: azimuth likelihood over 400 gradian bins (von Mises kernel), plus confidence.

2. Sector scheduler. Maintain a 400-bin bearing posterior fused from passive likelihoods and sonar contacts, with a diffusion step per second for target motion. Policy: scan the smallest sector containing 90 percent posterior mass plus a 5-degree margin, using ping-python `transmit_angle` per step; if confidence drops below threshold for N seconds, widen geometrically to full scan. Per-step cost is TOF at set range (~40 ms at 30 m) plus motor step, so a 40-degree sector revisits at ~2-3 s versus 25-35 s full sweep (Hansen 10609976 measured 9-32 s in a pool).

3. Contact extraction and track. Subtract an empty-pool reference scan (walls dominate at 750 kHz), threshold the residual polar profile in the scanned sector, take the range of the strongest blob within the passive bearing's HPD, and feed range-bearing into a constant-velocity Kalman filter in the vehicle frame. No learning is required for a first paper; a small learned contact detector on residual profiles is a stretch.
proposal.experiment_plan: Bench (week 1-2): measure speaker output spectrum with one hydrophone in a bucket; verify GCC-PHAT peak sharpness for chirp vs pink noise vs speech; confirm Ping360 sector control latency per step with ping-python. Pool session 1 (offline, ~3 h, 3 people: laptop operator, two on the speaker pole): sub static on the bottom at pool center with heading measured by compass and tape; take 3 empty-pool reference scans; hang the speaker on a weighted line from a pole at 24 static poses (8 bearings x 3 ranges: 3, 6, 10 m), depth matched to the sonar plane (Ping360 vertical fan is only 25 degrees), each pose playing 60 s of chirp + pink noise + speech; record both hydrophone streams and full 0.9-degree Ping360 scans. Ground truth: deck tape grid and plumb line (about 10 cm, ~1-2 degrees at 3 m). Offline outputs: passive bearing error vs range and signal type, sonar detectability of the speaker body vs pose, association success rate. Pool session 2 (closed loop): 8 moving trajectories (walk the pole along the deck at 0.3-0.5 m/s: arcs, radial approach, wall-hugging), each repeated under 5 policies: full 360 sweep, fixed forward 60-degree sector, sonar-only re-scan around last contact, random sector, passive-cued (ours). Ground truth for motion: overhead GoPro on a ladder tracking an AprilTag on a surface float on the suspension line, time-synced by a clap. Metrics: time-to-first-contact, mean revisit period, track-loss fraction, bearing RMSE (passive) and position RMSE (track) vs GT, fraction of scan budget spent within 10 degrees of target, plus a wall-echo false-contact rate. Session 3 (optional): thrusters on at low PWM to quantify self-noise degradation of the passive cue.
baselines: Full 360-degree Ping360 sweep at 0.9-degree step (Hansen 10609976 default), contact-then-track
Fixed forward sector (e.g. 60 degrees) with no cueing
Sonar-only adaptive re-scan around last contact (track-while-scan without passive cue): the key ablation
Random sector of equal width to the cued sector
Passive bearing only (no sonar): shows what the fusion adds in range and false-bearing rejection
Classical passive alternatives for the bearing stage: GCC-PHAT vs matched-filter first-peak vs SRP-PHAT over 4 channels once cross-board sync exists

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Active 3D localization of forward-looking-sonar-detected targets: a particle filter tracker plus deep RL chooses vehicle motions to resolve FLS elevation ambiguity (OCEANS Brest, initial study).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: They are sonar-only and act by moving the vehicle; we add an independent passive modality and act by steering the scan sector of a single-beam mechanical sonar, with the vehicle static. Their target has no acoustic emission.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Open-source ROS2 Ping360 + DVL mapping on a BlueROV2 (Raspberry Pi) using Synthetic Scan Formation and SLAM; measured 9-32 s per full scan in a pool and bunker.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: They always sweep full circles for mapping; we treat the mechanical scan as a controllable budget for target tracking and use hydrophones to allocate it. We reuse their scan-time numbers as the baseline cost model.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Synthetic Scan Formation: motion-compensated scan rendering for slow mechanical scanning sonars (IEEE Access).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Complementary: SSF fixes distortion from vehicle motion during a sweep; we shorten the sweep itself. No passive sensing in their work.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: 3-element hydrophone array with saliency-aware ConvLSTM DOA for 37.5/42 kHz ULD pulses; 4.97-degree MAE in lake trials; synchronous multi-channel ADC.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Their DOA is the end product; ours is a cue for an active sensor. They have a synchronous ADC; we work around unsynchronized boards with orthogonal intra-board pairs. Audio-band broadband source, reverberant pool, not deep lake.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Sparse-representation (OMP) multipath decomposition for pinger bearing with a 4-hydrophone square array, validated in a university swimming pool at 30 kHz.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Closest pool precedent for 4-hydrophone bearing; we borrow the earliest-path-is-LOS rule but add the active sonar loop and quantify tracking, not just static bearing.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: False-alarm reduction for active diver-detection sonar contacts via hand-crafted vs CNN classification (OCEANS Charleston).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Shows harbour-security active-sonar contact problems exist at scale; we use a passive cue rather than a classifier to reject clutter, on a low-cost single-beam sonar. Passive-cued active search is an old naval concept; our contribution is its quantitative low-cost embodiment with a scan-budget model.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: IoT tuna detection: cheap ultrasonic sensor triggers an underwater camera for classification.
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Same cheap-sensor-triggers-expensive-sensor pattern, but trigger only, no bearing, no sector steering, no tracking metrics.

closest_prior_work.what_they_did: Motion optimization for a team of AUVs doing passive acoustic monitoring and pursuit of a moving source with intermittent comms (JOE).
closest_prior_work.how_we_differ: Passive-only, multi-vehicle, simulation-scale; ours is single-vehicle sensor-level fusion with real hardware.

hardware_blockers: Two Daisy boards have no shared sample clock: each runs its own codec off its own crystal (verified in gen2/daisyseed_firmware; the only slave-to-master link is two analog DAC-to-ADC level lines, and stream_audio.cpp frames carry an 8-bit seq with no shared timebase; host arrival-time alignment jitters by ms, useless for TDOA where the whole baseline is ~200 us). Mitigation for a first result: use only intra-board pairs, mounted as orthogonal baselines (may require swapping two hydrophone cables so each board owns one diagonal; confirm current geometry). Stretch: master toggles a GPIO every 1024 samples, slave latches its audio sample counter on EXTI and reports pairs; host resamples slave stream piecewise-linearly (~50 lines of firmware per board). Crystal mismatch of ~50 ppm is ~5 samples/s at 96 kHz, so resync must be at least ~10 Hz.

Speaker band <= ~20 kHz and uncalibrated: not an interference issue for the 750 kHz Ping360, but narrowband tones above ~2.5 kHz phase-wrap on a ~0.3 m baseline, so the source file must be broadband (chirps/pink noise). Unknown source level and directivity limit passive range; characterize before session 1. The speaker is also the sonar target, so its housing must have usable target strength at 750 kHz and sit inside the 25-degree vertical fan; if returns are weak, hang a small metal reflector with it.
Pool walls at 750 kHz return far more energy than the target: requires an empty-pool reference scan and residual thresholding; targets within ~1-2 m of a wall will merge with wall returns.
Orin USB hub is documented as flaky (-71/-110 errors); two boards at 96 kHz/24-bit is ~1.15 MB/s total. Plan for 48 kHz/16-bit (sufficient for a <= 18 kHz source).

Ping360 command latency and serial throughput: each step is command-response; sector re-targeting after a large bearing jump costs a slew of ~1 s at 400 gradian resolution. No known Orin driver issue, but ping-python must be validated on aarch64.
Thruster self-noise will swamp the passive cue; first result must be with the vehicle static, which also removes the need for DVL/IMU motion compensation (Hansen SSF).
Ground truth for a moving target is the weakest link: overhead camera plus AprilTag float is cheap but needs a stable mount and time sync; budget a dry rehearsal.

Reviewers will note passive-cued active sonar is conceptually old in naval systems and that a pool is not a harbour; frame the contribution as a quantified scan-budget model for low-cost MSS with a hydrophone cue, and target the Aberdeen Underwater Security local track as secondary.
proposal.track: 02 Sonar Signal/Image Processing & Communication (array processing + sonar); secondary 10 Ocean Vehicles; also enter the Student Poster Competition. Local Underwater Security track is a plausible framing for harbour intruder/diver cueing.

evidence: Corpus (393 records in the search corpus): zero papers fuse a passive hydrophone array with a mechanically scanned sonar; the only Ping360 work is Hansen 10609976 / 10239384 (mapping, always full sweeps) and no paper steers an MSS sector from a passive cue. 3 IEEE API searches ('passive acoustic cueing active sonar bearing hydrophone', 'passive sonar cue active sonar', 'hydrophone scanning sonar fusion target tracking') returned 0, 1 (irrelevant BTSTNet 11478285), 0 hits.

The concept 'passive detection cues/narrows an active sonar search' is old and published: IEEE 6290467 'Active multistatic track initiation cued by passive acoustic detection' (FUSION 2012, Metron/ONR; passive CPA cue -> Gaussian-mixture hypotheses -> active track init, reports false-track reduction and cue hand-off, simulated data) and IEEE 6263410 'Passive acoustic tracking for cueing a multistatic active acoustic tracking system'; IEEE 4632243 'Cued passive bearing estimation in distributed sensor data fusion' (switch a sensor from full-azimuth surveillance to focused processing in the region of high contact probability). Reviewers from the sonar track will cite these and call D6 a low-cost re-embodiment.

Passive-hydrophone-triggered active sonar/camera acquisition is deployed hardware: Adaptable Monitoring Package, Polagye et al. 2020, J. Mar. Sci. Eng. 8(8):553 (doi 10.3390/jmse8080553) and OSTI 1618449 'Benchmarking sensor fusion capabilities of an integrated instrumentation package' (hydrophone array + multibeam + acoustic camera, event-triggered acquisition). Commercial: Forcys Sentinel 2 SInAPS (simultaneous in-band active+passive intruder sonar). Trigger only, fixed beams, no sector steering, but it undercuts 'first passive-cued active sensing on cheap hardware'.

Robot audition already does 'mic array bearing steers a narrow-FOV active/visual sensor': Nakadai et al. active audition (ICSLP 2002, J. JSAI 2003), ARL impulsive-noise detection cueing a pan-tilt camera, 'Audio-visual attention control of a pan-tilt telepresence robot'. Jahromi Shirazi & Abaid 2021, IET RSN 15:... 'Eavesdropping like a bat: fusing active and passive sonar for SLAM' explicitly motivates fusing passive listening with a slow scanning active sonar (simulation only, in-air). The idea of using passive DOA to save scan time is therefore not new in robotics; only the underwater/MSS instantiation is.

The headline number is arithmetically foregone: a 40-degree sector vs 360 degrees at fixed per-step cost is 9x faster by construction; Hansen 10609976 already measured 9-32 s per full Ping360 sweep. A reviewer will say time-to-contact/revisit 'order of magnitude' improvements are a property of the sector width chosen, not a finding, so the experiment as designed mostly confirms the cost model rather than testing a hypothesis.

Closest local competitor at the venue: Hasan, Kannan, Rohan, Talaat 2025, 'Interpreting navigation sonar data for object detection: a feasibility study using the Ping360', J. Supercomputing 81:1616 (Robert Gordon Univ. / Univ. of Aberdeen; controlled pool experiments, U-Net on Ping360 profiles). Aberdeen reviewers will know Ping360-in-pool work and will judge the sonar-side contribution against it.

Abdullah, Blow, Rampazzi, Islam, 'Active localization of close-range adversarial acoustic sources for underwater data center surveillance', IEEE JOE 2026 (arnumber 11615015; arXiv 2510.20122): fixed + robot-mounted hydrophones, LC-MAP prior + UKF, Gazebo + open-water trials, 3D position and velocity of an emitting source in real time. Passive-only (no active sonar) but it is the current state of the art for 'robot localizes an acoustic emitter with few hydrophones and tracks it', and its tracking metrics are stronger than a two-pair GCC-PHAT bearing.

Cecchi et al. 11104638 (OCEANS Brest 2025) and Tiranti 11164337 (JOE 2025) already occupy 'active sensing policy for underwater target localization' at OCEANS; D6 must be positioned as sensor-level budget allocation, not as a new active-perception paradigm.
votes.fix: Not refuted outright (nobody has published a hydrophone-cued mechanically-scanned sonar with closed-loop pool metrics), but as proposed it is an engineering demo of a known naval/robotics concept whose headline 'order of magnitude' metric is fixed by the sector width. To survive: (1) drop the 9x speedup as the claim and make the contribution the things prior work does not have: a scan-budget model for single-beam MSS (per-step cost = TOF + motor step) with a regret-vs-oracle metric and a measured break-even curve of passive bearing error/confidence vs sector width and track-loss, i.e. 'how good must the cue be before cueing beats sonar-only track-while-scan'; (2) make the sonar-only adaptive re-scan (track-while-scan) the primary baseline and show where it fails (initial acquisition, wall-merged contacts, target manoeuvre) and where the passive cue rescues it, since that comparison is the only non-trivial result; (3) sell the clock-free orthogonal intra-board GCC-PHAT bearing in a six-wall reverberant pool with matched-filter first-peak selection as a stand-alone measured result (bearing error vs range/signal type), because unsynchronized-board DOA in a pool is itself unpublished; (4) cite 6290467/6263410/4632243, AMP (jmse8080553) and robot audition up front and frame the paper as 'the first quantitative embodiment on a $2k MSS + 4 hydrophones on an AUV, with open code', targeting Track 02 plus the Student Poster Competition rather than a headline full paper; keep P1 as the headline and D6 as the second/poster paper, as 00_directions.md already ranks it.

votes.lens: Feasibility / pool-test engineering (D6: passive hydrophone bearing steers Ping360 sector)
evidence: Headline metric is true by construction and undersized at pool ranges. Blue Robotics spec: full 360 scan is 4.2 s at 1 m range, 33 s at 50 m; Hansen 10609976 measured 9-32 s across step/intensity settings. In a ~25 m pool with the sub at centre, usable range is <=6 m laterally / <=12 m along the length, so a full sweep is ~6-12 s, not the proposal's 25-35 s (that is the 50 m figure). Revisit-period ratio = sector fraction (40/360), so 'order of magnitude' is arithmetic, not a finding; expected time-to-first-contact for the full-sweep baseline is ~half a sweep (~3-6 s) vs ~1 s cued. The key ablation (sonar-only track-while-scan re-scan around last contact) gets the same revisit reduction once acquired: at 0.3-0.5 m/s and ~1-2 s revisit the target moves <=1 m, i.e. <=12 deg at 5 m, well inside a 40 deg window. What survives is acquisition time and wall-clutter rejection, a much smaller claim.

Array geometry is wrong for the proposed method. gen2/daisyseed_firmware/master_ros.cpp line 84-90 and master_ping.cpp: 'front = hydrophones 0 and 3, back = 1 and 2 (0/1 = master codec inputs, 2/3 = slave)'. Both intra-board pairs are therefore PARALLEL fore-aft baselines, giving only cos(theta) each with an unresolved left/right ambiguity. Orthogonal diagonals require physically re-cabling two hydrophones through the hull (H0+H2 on master, H1+H3 on slave), on the only working vehicle, before session 1. No hydrophone spacing is documented anywhere in the repo, so bearing resolution cannot yet be predicted (at 48 kHz and ~0.3 m it is ~6 deg per sample at broadside, worse toward endfire; sub-sample interpolation needed to get the 5 deg margin the scheduler assumes).

The static 8 bearings x 3 ranges (3/6/10 m) grid and the moving trajectories (arcs, radial approach) are not reachable from the deck with the sub at pool centre: a 25 m pool is typically ~12.5 m wide, so 10 m range from centre is outside the pool on the width axis, and every deck-walked trajectory is by definition a 'wall-hugging' trajectory (target 1-3 m from a concrete wall, where the proposal itself says target and wall returns merge at 750 kHz). Nobody in a 3-person crew can hold a 10 cm-accurate static pose while treading water. Prior pool precedent (Kasetkasem 8096292) used only 5 static pinger locations with a fixed array, no motion, no closed loop.

Moving-target ground truth as planned does not cover the experiment. A GoPro on a ladder ~3 m above the water sees roughly 6 x 4 m of surface; the 8 trajectories at 3-10 m range span 20 m of pool. AprilTag on a surface float attached to a hanging speaker also lags/pendulums relative to the submerged target by tens of cm at 0.3-0.5 m/s, comparable to the range resolution being claimed for the track RMSE.

Sonar clutter geometry with the vehicle on the bottom: Ping360 vertical fan is 25 deg, so with the transducer ~0.3 m above the floor the entire floor is inside the fan beyond ~1.4 m, and at ~2 m depth the surface enters the fan beyond ~8 m. The target hangs in the floor-clutter band at every range; reference-scan subtraction handles a static floor but not the surface (people, ripples), and the speaker's 750 kHz target strength is unmeasured. Minimum range 0.75 m (transducer ringdown) is fine, but this needs the sub raised on a crate/stand, which the plan does not include.

Self-noise coupling not considered: the Ping360 stepper motor and transmit electronics are on the same hull within ~0.5 m of audio-band hydrophones and step at ~10-40 Hz continuously during a scan; mechanical stepping is audible in the 0-20 kHz band the passive cue uses. The closed loop must either gate the passive estimate between steps (halving its duty cycle) or measure/subtract the coupling; unverified and not in the bench plan.

Software gap: there is zero Ping360 / ping-python / brping code anywhere in the repo, no speaker make/model or measured response, no hydrophone spacing, and the repo documents the Orin USB hub as unreliable (gen2/README.md: '-71/-110 errors', port assignment is load-bearing). Adding a third USB serial device (Ping360) plus two Daisy streams at 48 kHz on that hub is a plausible multi-week bring-up on its own; the 6-week first-result estimate assumes it works first try.

Corpus check (393 unique IEEE records in the search corpus): no record combines a hydrophone cue with mechanical-scanning-sonar sector steering (closest: 10239384, 10609976 mapping; 7778656 MSS iceberg profiling), so novelty is not the blocker; the blocker is that the achievable demonstration is a small-range, static-vehicle, near-wall acquisition test, and the proposed headline number is a scan-fraction identity.
